items.title: Cade Cavalli, Nationals seek rare 2026 win vs. Marlins
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Washington Nationals recently completed a stretch of games in which they went 3-12 and saw their National League wild-card hopes fall by the wayside.
items.body:
The Washington Nationals recently completed a stretch of games in which they went 3-12 and saw their National League wild-card hopes fall by the wayside.
That stretch of games could be divided into two categories: games started by right-hander Cade Cavalli (in which they went 3-0) and games started by somebody else (0-12).
Washington just ended that pattern with two straight wins, and the red-hot Cavalli will try to make it three in a row when the Nationals host the Miami Marlins in the second of a four-game series on Saturday.
Cavalli (12-5, 3.21 ERA) will face a formidable mound opponent as right-hander Sandy Alcantara (13-8, 3.38) goes for Miami.
Alcantara, in his second season back from Tommy John surgery, is returning to his Cy Young Award form. The 30-year-old has allowed either one or zero runs in seven of his past 10 starts, while lowering his ERA from 4.20 as it stood on June 29.
Last time out, he gave up one run on six hits in seven innings against the Boston Red Sox on Monday. He took a no-decision in the 4-2 loss.
"We're counting on him to go deep into this one and give us a chance, and that's what he did," manager Clayton McCullough said. "Unfortunate to get a quality start like that again from him and not be able to forge ahead and take control of the game. But he did all that he could."
Alcantara is 9-6 with a 3.57 ERA in 18 starts against Washington, including 1-0 with a 3.46 ERA in two starts this season.
The holder of several team pitching records, Alcantara will claim another on Saturday when he makes his 198th start for the Marlins, passing Ricky Nolasco for sole possession of the franchise record for most starts.
The 28-year-old Cavalli has made just 39 career starts. He is 4-0 with a 1.73 ERA and 36 strikeouts in 26 innings over his past four. Last time out he allowed two runs on five hits in six innings against the Rockies, a 13-3 win. It was his ninth straight quality start, a stretch in which he is 7-1 with one no-decision.
"Cade continues to be that guy where when we need to get going again, it seems like it's his turn to pitch," manager Blake Butera said. "He just continues to pick us up at big times, and stop some bad momentum at times and get us back on track."
Cavalli is 0-0 with a 3.38 ERA in two starts versus Miami this season. On May 10, the Nationals lost 5-2, and also took a 7-3 loss to the Marlins on June 1. He didn't get a decision in either game.
Rookie Jackson Kent was the Washington pitching star Friday night, allowing one run on three hits in seven innings to earn his first major league win in his fourth career start.
"What an outing," Butera said. "Picked us up when we really needed it. Bullpen was thin going into tonight. Obviously playing a ton of games in a row. ... It was impressive stuff."
Brady House hit a three-run homer, and Harry Ford added a solo shot as the Nationals won their second game in a row for the first time since Aug. 7-9. Washington ended an eight-game losing streak against Miami and is 2-8 against the Marlins on the season.
Heriberto Hernandez homered for the Marlins, who have lost three of four.
Marlins starter Eury Perez lasted just three innings, allowing five runs on two hits and four walks.
"Really just a lack of command tonight and unable to make enough pitches," McCullough said.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Islandia vota sobre si iniciar las negociaciones para la adhesión a la UE
items.author: Tom Little, Johan Ahlander
items.creator: Tom Little, Johan Ahlander
items.summary: Los islandeses votaban el sábado sobre la reapertura de las negociaciones de adhesión a la Unión Europea, con la población dividida a partes iguales tras una campaña centrada en el costo de la vida, la seguridad, la soberanía y el control sobre las aguas pesqueras.
items.body:
Los islandeses votaban el sábado sobre la reapertura de las negociaciones de adhesión a la Unión Europea, con la población dividida a partes iguales tras una campaña centrada en el costo de la vida, la seguridad, la soberanía y el control sobre las aguas pesqueras.
El resultado es demasiado reñido como para dar un ganador. Una encuesta de Gallup publicada el viernes sugería que una estrecha mayoría se oponía a reabrir las negociaciones, lo que supone un ligero cambio respecto a sondeos anteriores que apuntaban a una ligera ventaja para los partidarios de reanudar las conversaciones.
Los defensores del "sí", que respaldan las negociaciones, afirman que la adhesión al bloque podría aliviar las altas tasas de interés y ofrecer más seguridad en un mundo convulso por la guerra en Ucrania y las amenazas del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, sobre otra isla ártica, Groenlandia.
Los defensores del "no" argumentan que la adhesión a la UE amenazaría la soberanía de la isla y sus aguas pesqueras.
"Hoy es nuestro encuentro con la historia", afirmó el expresidente de Islandia, Ólafur Ragnar Grímsson, opositor a la adhesión a la UE, en una publicación en las redes sociales.
Si los votantes dijeran "sí", eso solo abriría la vía a las negociaciones con Bruselas. Islandia tendría entonces que celebrar un segundo referéndum, probablemente varios años después, sobre si entrar al bloque.
VIEJAS PREGUNTAS, NUEVA URGENCIA Islandia solicitó por primera vez su adhesión a la UE en 2009, en plena crisis financiera que afectó con especial dureza a la pequeña y vulnerable economía del país. Las negociaciones concluyeron en 2013, cuando un gobierno euroescéptico archivó el proceso.
La renovada agitación geopolítica ha aportado una nueva urgencia a una cuestión que los islandeses llevan décadas debatiendo de forma intermitente.
La ministra de Relaciones Exteriores, Thorgerdur Katrin Gunnarsdottir, que ha respaldado el "sí", declaró a Reuters la semana pasada que la votación se reduce a una sencilla pregunta: ¿puede Islandia seguir permitiéndose mantenerse al margen en un mundo en el que las viejas certezas se están desmoronando?
"El orden internacional que ha sustentado nuestra seguridad y prosperidad durante décadas se encuentra bajo una fuerte presión", afirmó. "En tiempos como estos, las naciones pequeñas deben reflexionar detenidamente sobre cuál es su posición y quién está de su lado".
TASAS DE INTERÉS Y COSTO DE LA VIDA Los debates en Islandia se han centrado más en las tasas de interés, los derechos de pesca y el costo de la vida que en la seguridad.
Islandia se ha enfrentado a una inflación persistentemente alta y a tasas que han encarecido de forma desmesurada las hipotecas, y los partidarios del "sí" afirman que la adhesión a la UE, y posiblemente la adopción del euro, podrían suponer un cierto alivio. El tipo del banco central de Islandia se sitúa en el 8%, frente al 2,25% del Banco Central Europeo.
"No resolvería los problemas estructurales de Islandia, pero podría convertirse en un catalizador para una economía más saludable", afirmó Vilhjalmur Hilmarsson, economista jefe de Viska, uno de los sindicatos más grandes de Islandia.
La líder de la oposición, Gudrun Hafsteinsdottir, que ha encabezado la campaña por el "no", afirma que se exagera la importancia de los argumentos económicos. "Estos no son problemas que Bruselas vaya a resolver por nosotros. Son problemas que deben resolver los políticos islandeses", afirmó.
LA PESCA, EL PUNTO DE FRICCIÓN Según la normativa de la UE, las cuotas de pesca se basan, entre otras cosas, en los patrones históricos de capturas. Algunos responsables sostienen que eso permitiría a Islandia mantener el control de sus aguas, ya que ningún país de la UE ha pescado allí desde hace décadas.
Los detractores no están convencidos. "Sé que la Unión Europea ofrecerá algunas promesas de flexibilidad, sobre todo al principio, pero sabemos que no será para siempre", señaló Hafsteinsdottir.
Un memorándum del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores estima que las negociaciones de adhesión podrían comenzar a fines de 2026 y durar entre 18 y 24 meses, si la votación del sábado se pronuncia a favor de reabrir las negociaciones.
Islandia también debe celebrar elecciones generales antes de noviembre de 2028, lo que añade una nueva capa de incertidumbre política a cualquier calendario de negociaciones que se prolongue hasta ese periodo.
Los colegios electorales abrieron a las 0900 GMT en todo el país, que cuenta con unos 400.000 habitantes. Está previsto que cierren a las 2200 GMT.

items.title: Ataque ruso contra almacén en área de Kiev provoca explosión que se cobra la vida de 37 personas
items.author: Dan Peleschuk
items.creator: Dan Peleschuk
items.summary: Al menos 37 personas perdieron la vida después de que un ataque con drones rusos contra un almacén en las afueras de Kiev provocara una explosión, según informaron las autoridades el sábado, mientras los ataques aéreos de Moscú contra la capital ucraniana y sus alrededores se prolongaban por tercer día consecutivo.
items.body:
Al menos 37 personas perdieron la vida después de que un ataque con drones rusos contra un almacén en las afueras de Kiev provocara una explosión, según informaron las autoridades el sábado, mientras los ataques aéreos de Moscú contra la capital ucraniana y sus alrededores se prolongaban por tercer día consecutivo.
El presidente Volodímir Zelenski prometió castigar a los responsables de la explosión del almacén ocurrida a última hora del viernes, que causó uno de los mayores números de víctimas mortales en meses y que parece ser el segundo incidente de este tipo en dos meses.
Decenas de personas resultaron heridas y más de 370 fueron evacuadas de la zona del ataque en la localidad de Myla, según indicó Zelenski. Las infraestructuras cercanas sufrieron "daños importantes", añadió, entre ellas edificios residenciales y un centro de atención a personas mayores.
"Quienes permitieron que esto ocurriera deben rendir cuentas por sus decisiones", escribió Zelenski en la red social X. "Existen normativas vigentes: no se puede almacenar munición cerca de viviendas u otras zonas residenciales. Sin duda, se sacarán las conclusiones pertinentes".
Rusia ha intensificado su guerra aérea contra Ucrania, utilizando más misiles balísticos y drones propulsados por reactores que son difíciles de derribar.
Otras nueve regiones fueron blanco de ataques nocturnos por parte de Rusia, añadió Zelenski, señalando que Kiev, en particular, estaba sometida a un "ataque prácticamente incesante" de drones de alta velocidad.
El sábado, las sirenas sonaron durante toda la mañana por tercer día consecutivo, mientras la fuerza aérea ucraniana advertía de nuevas oleadas de drones que se acercaban a la capital. El estruendo de los sistemas de defensa aérea resonaba en el cielo.
El gobernador de la región de Kiev, Tymur Tkachenko, afirmó que una niña de 14 años falleció en un ataque con drones perpetrado por la mañana en el distrito de Boryspil. En Kiev, una niña de dos años murió al caer un dron, según declaró el sábado el alcalde Vitali Klitschko.
Los ataques en Kiev y sus alrededores, el jueves y el viernes, habían causado daños en almacenes y viviendas, lo que, según algunos responsables ucranianos, forma parte de una campaña destinada a "paralizar" esta ciudad de varios millones de habitantes.
La explosión del viernes se produce tras un incidente similar ocurrido el mes pasado en la localidad de Vyshneve, en las afueras de Kiev, donde 10 personas perdieron la vida y cientos de viviendas resultaron dañadas después de que un ataque provocara explosiones secundarias.
"En el quinto año de guerra a gran escala, no tenemos derecho a permitir que se repitan tragedias como la ocurrida en Vyshneve y esta otra en el distrito de Bucha", publicó en Telegram el primer ministro Sergiy Koretskyi, quien visitó el lugar de la explosión del viernes.
Zelenski afirmó que ya se habían abierto causas penales por negligencia en el ejercicio de funciones. Las autoridades ucranianas rara vez revelan los daños causados a objetivos militares por los ataques rusos.

items.title: Fresh off rout, Mariners seek to even with Blue Jays
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The visiting Seattle Mariners aim to square their three-game series with the Toronto Blue Jays on Saturday afternoon and avoid falling farther back in the chase for a postseason berth.
items.body:
The visiting Seattle Mariners aim to square their three-game series with the Toronto Blue Jays on Saturday afternoon and avoid falling farther back in the chase for a postseason berth.
The Blue Jays recorded an 8-1 win in the series opener on Friday to even the season series between the teams at 2-2.
The Mariners are four games out of first in the American League West and four games in back of the third wild-card spot.
The Blue Jays moved to within 2 1/2 games of the third AL wild-card slot.
The win in the series opener was a big turnaround from Toronto's 13-2 loss to the Kansas City Royals on Thursday. The home crowd booed the Blue Jays out of the building.
On Friday, Toronto answered Dominic Canzone's homer in the first with three runs in the bottom of the inning.
"That's a really good bounce-back win," Blue Jays manager John Schneider said. "It was nice to answer right back in the first inning. We talked to the guys today. We've got 26 games left, hopefully more. Let's worry about one day at a time and leave it all out there."
Dylan Cease struck out eight batters in six innings for the Blue Jays to strengthen his case at the American League Cy Young Award.
"They all feel like must-wins at this point," Cease said. "We didn't play as well against Kansas City and now we're trying to gain ground and set the tone. It's crunch time and there are not a lot of games left."
George Springer homered among his four hits for Toronto.
Right-hander Jose Soriano (10-7, 3.43 ERA) is Toronto's expected starter on Saturday. He is 2-1 with a 3.46 ERA in 11 career games (six starts) against the Mariners and 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA in one start this season.
Rookie left-hander Kade Anderson (0-0, 4.76) is listed to make his second career start for the Mariners. In his major league debut, he allowed three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings last Saturday. He did not factor into the decision in Seattle's 5-4 victory.
Mariners manager Dan Wilson said on Friday that right-hander Bryce Miller will move to the bullpen.
"It's definitely on a short-term basis, and a chance for him to go down, and make some adjustments and get back on track in some way," Wilson said. "Bryce is going to be a pitcher for us for a long time, win a lot of games for us."
Seattle starter Emerson Hancock limped slightly after making a tag on Nathan Lukes's grounder in the first inning on Friday. After being checked by a trainer the right-hander continued and allowed five runs in five innings.
"He kind of tweaked his groin a bit," Wilson said.
"It felt weird," Hancock said. "Just something that I feel like I needed to be able to kind of get through to be able to try and get as many outs and innings as I could. We'll kind of see tomorrow how everything's feeling."
Toronto recalled CJ Van Eyk on Friday and he pitched around a walk in the ninth. Fellow right-hander Simeon Woods Richardson was designated for assignment.
Seattle infielder Brendan Donovan is with the team and is eligible to leave the seven-day concussion injured list on Saturday. Wilson, however, said that he does not feel Donovan will be ready to return that soon.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Reds, Sal Stewart look to continue torrid hitting against Cubs
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Cincinnati Reds have ignited their offense in back-to-back games after it had been dormant far too many times over the last 2 1/2 weeks.
items.body:
The Cincinnati Reds have ignited their offense in back-to-back games after it had been dormant far too many times over the last 2 1/2 weeks.
Fresh off erupting for 10 runs in consecutive contests, the visiting Reds will look to continue swinging hot bats on Saturday afternoon when they face the Chicago Cubs.
Cincinnati scored seven runs in the ninth inning to secure a 10-9 victory over the San Francisco Giants on Thursday. On Friday, the Reds belted four homers to pick up a 10-8 win over the Cubs in the opener of a three-game series.
That's not too shabby considering Cincinnati had scored one or fewer runs in nine of its previous 17 games.
"We're just playing hard. Shows the resilience of this team," rookie Sal Stewart said. ... "We're going out there playing to win. I'm glad we're playing hard because that's the standard that we have."
Stewart launched his team-leading 29th homer of the season on Friday to give him his 101st RBI, breaking the franchise rookie record previously held by Jim Greengrass, who had 100 RBIs in 1953.
"You've got to drive in runs to win the game," said Stewart, who added the go-ahead RBI single in the sixth inning.
Tyler Stephenson launched a three-run blast, while Jose Trevino and TJ Friedl each added solo shots.
Rookie Hector Rodriguez added an RBI single to extend his hitting streak to six games.
While Cincinnati has reason to feel good, Chicago has lost three in a row and six of its last eight games.
Although his team is struggling, Michael Busch has been heating up at the plate.
Busch belted a two-run homer in the third inning on Friday to mark the third time that he has gone deep in his last nine games. He also has three doubles and eight walks in that span.
Keeping Busch in check will be the responsibility of Cincinnati left-hander Andrew Abbott (6-9, 4.15 ERA), who will get the start on Saturday afternoon.
Abbott has dropped his last two starts after allowing four runs on seven hits in six innings in a 5-3 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks last Sunday.
He recorded a pair of no-decisions against Chicago this season, tossing 5 2/3 scoreless innings on May 5 and yielding four runs in four frames on July 12.
Abbott, 27, is 3-1 with a 2.79 ERA in nine career appearances (all starts) versus the Cubs.
Chicago right-hander Kevin Gausman (7-11, 4.37 ERA) will get the nod on Saturday afternoon.
Gausman scattered three hits over seven scoreless innings against the Diamondbacks on Monday to record his third win in his last five outings dating back to his last start with the Toronto Blue Jays.
"He's a good energy guy, the work ethic is there," catcher Carson Kelly said of Gausman. "I mean, he's been doing this for such a long time and he's a true pro and he wants the ball. You can see that every inning. It just seems like he gets stronger and stronger, and that's something that our guys can really look at and build off of."
Gausman, 35, is 1-4 with a 7.89 ERA in six career appearances (all starts) versus the Reds.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Three Finance Ministers on Avoiding Debt Crises
items.summary: US public debt just crossed $40 trillion, but the country is hardly the only one facing fiscal troubles. Nations around the world took on record debt during Covid, and many have struggled to bring spending back under control. Chrystia Freeland, who faced this problem herself as Canada's Finance Minister, speaks with former Dutch Finance Minister Sigrid Kaag and former German Finance Minister Christian Lindner about why fiscal discipline is so politically difficult and what the rest of the world can learn before markets force the issue. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: As White Sox chase division title, Twins continue youth movement
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Minnesota Twins top prospect Walker Jenkins played his first big-league game and ripped his first big-league hit.
items.body:
Minnesota Twins top prospect Walker Jenkins played his first big-league game and ripped his first big-league hit.
Now, he is looking to experience his first victory in the majors.
Jenkins and the Twins will look to pull even in the series when they go up against the Chicago White Sox on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis. The White Sox are coming off a 7-4 win in the series opener Friday night.
The next game will mark another opportunity for Jenkins, a 21-year-old who went 1-for-3 in his debut. The Twins selected Jenkins in the first round (No. 5 overall) out of high school in North Carolina in 2023.
"The guy's a stud," teammate Luke Keaschall said. "I'm just happy I get to play with him now, and I'm super happy to watch his career play out."
Meanwhile, the White Sox will try to leave Jenkins winless in his opening weekend. They have won three games in a row and four of their past five, and they will look to increase their lead atop the American League Central as the postseason approaches.
White Sox right-hander Erick Fedde (6-8, 4.18 ERA) is set to take the mound on Saturday. He is looking for his first victory since July 31 against the Tampa Bay Rays.
In his most recent start last Sunday, Fedde pitched four scoreless innings against the New York Mets and drew a no-decision in the 2-1 win. He scattered three hits, walked one and struck out two.
Fedde is 3-0 with a 0.96 ERA in five career starts against Minnesota. He has allowed only three runs in 28 innings, and he has walked six and struck out 27 in those starts. One of those victories came June 3, when Fedde allowed just two hits over five innings in an 8-0 win.
Minnesota plans to counter with right-hander Bailey Ober (7-4, 4.49). He is hoping to notch his first victory since July 17, when he defeated the Chicago Cubs.
Ober has not surpassed five innings in either of his past two starts. During his most recent outing last Sunday, he allowed one run on four hits in five innings against the San Diego Padres. He took a no-decision in the 8-1 loss.
In 15 career starts against the White Sox, Ober is 6-2 with a 3.67 ERA.
The White Sox moved to a season-high eight games over .500 on Friday and now lead the American League Central by 3 1/2 games over the Cleveland Guardians. The Twins have lost three consecutive games and stand 7 1/2 games behind the White Sox but have a chance to close the gap. The teams will meet five more times between now and Sept. 6.
White Sox outfielder Sam Antonacci will look to make a difference on the basepaths in the second game of the series. He swiped his 17th base of the season Friday night.
"The thing about Sammy that we all love is that he plays hard every single moment that he's out there," White Sox manager Will Venable said. "However that takes shape is fine with me as long as he's OK."
The Twins will try to battle back as their youth movement takes shape.
Shortstop Kaelen Culpepper is coming off a productive series opener in which he went 1-for-3 with a walk. He is hitting .333 in 17 games since his promotion earlier this month, and he is excited to welcome Jenkins into the fold.
"We kind of joked about it, like we were hitting 1 and 2 in (Triple-A) Saint Paul. Now we're hitting 8 and 9 (with the Twins)," Culpepper said. "Going back to (2024), when we played together in high-Class A, when I first played with him, we talked about our future together. ... Now, it's a reality. It's a pretty cool thing."

items.title: Dodgers' Blake Snell strives to continue good form vs. Tigers
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Blake Snell has delivered three quality starts this month for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
items.body:
Blake Snell has delivered three quality starts this month for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
The veteran left-hander will look to continue that streak in Detroit on Saturday afternoon against the Tigers.
Snell's return from an elbow injury was delayed until earlier this month. He had begun the season on the injured list with left shoulder fatigue before making one start May 9. He subsequently underwent surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. He's quickly reestablished himself as one of the top pitchers in the majors.
He's given up just two runs and seven hits while recording 21 strikeouts in 18 innings over his last three outings. Snell (2-1, 2.57 ERA) held Pittsburgh to two hits over six scoreless innings on Sunday while collecting his second straight victory.
However, Snell was far from satisfied with his performance. He issued three two-out walks, preventing him from going deeper into the game.
"It's not acceptable," Snell said. "I feel good, I know I can command the ball. Honestly, it's lazy. It's me trying to get strikeouts instead of trying to go seven, eight, nine. So, I definitely got to clean that up."
Snell missed a good chunk of last season, then pitched well down the stretch and won three consecutive playoff starts.
"I think he's had a lot of practice in going from one mode to another," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Like he told me, his words: 'It's the playoffs for me, right now from the outset.' So he's showing that. The games are going to get more intense as we get into September and beyond. But love what we see."
Snell faced the Tigers early last season, giving up two runs in five innings. He's 1-2 with a 5.48 ERA in four career appearances (all starts) against Detroit.
Right-hander Keider Montero (9-8, 3.30) will start for Detroit. Montero hasn't pitched since giving up three runs in five innings at Pittsburgh on Aug. 18. All those runs scored in the fifth inning.
The Tigers decided to skip Montero's next scheduled start after he showed signs of fatigue. He has pitched a career-high 133 2/3 innings in the majors this season.
"We're paying attention to his recovery coming off his last outing," manager A.J. Hinch said early this week. "He had that long inning and the recovery hasn't been fast. ... We're just giving him a blow. It's not uncommon this time of year, especially with the off days coming up. We're trying to be smart, pushing these guys when they need to be pushed, but also pulling back when they need to be pulled back."
Montero faced the Dodgers once during his rookie year in 2024, giving up five runs in five innings.
The Tigers have lost eight of their last nine games, including the series opener on Friday. Freddie Freeman knocked in the go-ahead run in the eighth inning of the Dodgers' 2-1 victory.
Los Angeles, which snapped a three-game losing streak, left 15 runners on base. But the Tigers couldn't take advantage as they were held to five hits and struck out 12 times. Detroit was blanked in its previous game against Tampa Bay.
Saturday's game figures to be less emotionally charged. Former Tigers ace Tarik Skubal pitched at Comerica Park for the first time since he was traded earlier this month. He gave up one run in six innings and wound up with a no-decision.
--Field Level Media

DUBAI: Iranian leaders are acknowledging the economic toll of war with the United States, with the supreme leader urging the government to address the hardship and the president saying foreign trade has shrunk by a third due to the American sanctions and blockade.
Yet Tehran signalled no retreat on Saturday (Aug 29), vowing to withstand US pressure, pursue diplomacy and maintain what it said was control over the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway giving Iran leverage through its ability to disrupt global energy markets.
The government said in a statement on state media that addressing economic pressures caused by sanctions and war was a central focus, including curbing inflation, managing markets, creating jobs, directing investment towards domestic production and gradually reducing dependence on the dollar.
Six months after the US and Israel launched the war, negotiations are at an impasse , and US President Donald Trump's administration has stepped up efforts to punish Iran financially with what it has billed as an "economic D-Day".

SANCTIONS COMPOUND TOLL ON IRAN'S ECONOMY Washington has warned countries to cut business ties with Iran or face secondary sanctions, though the Treasury Department stopped short of imposing penalties against major Iranian trade partners such as China and India, which could have repercussions for the US and global economies.
The Treasury imposed sanctions on Egypt's Banque Misr for doing business with Tehran, proposing a rule that would cut off the bank's branches in the United Arab Emirates from dollar transactions.
Egypt's central bank said it and the foreign ministry were in contact with US officials concerning the matter, adding the measure was limited to Banque Misr UAE’s US dollar transactions with correspondent banks only.
Banque Misr said later in a statement it was reviewing the US Treasury notice, adding that its branch in the UAE continued to provide banking services to its customers in line with applicable rules and procedures.
The US also issued sanctions targeting an entity based in Hong Kong and a person linked to Iran's Bank Melli, according to a notice on the Treasury website.
The sanctions drive compounds the toll of the war on Iran's economy, where annual inflation hit 66 per cent last month.
Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei - who has not been seen publicly since he was injured in the initial Feb 28 attack that killed his father and former Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei - called on the government to tackle the economic hardship.
"There is the need to seriously address the chain of economic and livelihood challenges, such as inflation, unemployment, management of prices and the market for goods and services," according to a written statement attributed to Khamenei.
President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that Iranian exports and imports had slumped nearly 35 per cent because of US sanctions and a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
But he said Iran was able to sell about 90 million barrels of oil during the short-lived memorandum of understanding that the US and Iran signed in June, when Washington permitted Iranian oil sales.

Related:

China says US 'sanctions and pressure' on Iran not a solution

China says its cooperation with Iran should not be disrupted

IRAN VOWS TO PURSUE DIPLOMACY AND DEFENCE With the US focused on its economic pressure campaign, others have sought to revive diplomatic efforts to end the war.
Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed Abdulrahman Al Thani met with Iranian leaders in Tehran on Thursday. He said he had stressed during the meeting the importance of returning to the pre-war status of open shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Friday described the talks with Al Thani as "creative".
In Saturday's statement, Iran said diplomacy and defence were "two complementary, coordinated and inseparable wings" for protecting the country's national interests, security and territorial integrity. It said it would pursue both tracks in a balanced manner.
Qatar, a US ally and Gulf neighbour to Iran, and Pakistan helped broker the June memorandum of understanding that led to a brief ceasefire before disagreements over the vital strait caused it to unravel. Before the war, the waterway carried 20 per cent of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas.
US military commanders say American forces have cleared sea mines from the strait that had been laid months ago by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
Trump has repeatedly said the Strait of Hormuz is open, but the Revolutionary Guards' navy said in a statement that such claims "are an obvious lie", reiterating that the waterway remained closed to ships without Iranian permission.
Only seven commodity vessels transited the strait on Thursday, down from 17 a day earlier and below the 10-day average of 15, preliminary shipping data showed on Friday.

Source: Reuters/rl

items.title: Yankees lean on pitching ahead of doubleheader vs. Red Sox
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox offered a glimpse at what a postseason encounter might look like on Friday night.
items.body:
The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox offered a glimpse at what a postseason encounter might look like on Friday night.
After widening their lead in the race for the American League's top wild-card spot, the Yankees hope to see standout showings from Carlos Rodon and Max Fried when they host the Red Sox in a day-night doubleheader on Saturday.
New York moved three games ahead of the Red Sox when Cam Schlittler and three relievers combined on a five-hitter in Friday's 1-0 victory. Cody Bellinger threw out Ceddanne Rafaela at the plate as the potential tying run in the seventh inning.
New York enters its third doubleheader since the All-Star break with a major league-best 3.22 ERA despite spending time without Gerrit Cole, Rodon and Fried.
In the opener, Rodon (4-2, 3.15 ERA) will make his third start since returning from a second injured list stint due to elbow inflammation. He likely will see his pitch count gradually increase.
Rodon threw 66 pitches in his return on Aug. 18 at Baltimore and increased to 76 Sunday when he allowed two runs on two hits in four innings during New York's 8-3 win over Toronto.
The left-hander is 5-6 with a 3.98 ERA in 13 career starts against Boston.
In the nightcap, Fried (4-4, 2.81) will return from a second but much shorter injured list stint due to a bone bruise in his left elbow.
Fried last pitched Aug. 13 and allowed a solo homer to Weston Wilson among five hits in five innings in 1-0 loss to the Seattle Mariners. Fried was 0-1 with a 1.82 ERA in five starts after returning from his initial two-month absence before being placed on the injured list Aug. 17.
The left-hander is 4-1 with a 1.88 ERA in six career starts against Boston.
"He has responded well," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said of Fried. "Actually, similar to how he responded the first time when he left Baltimore and missed more time. He has kind of responded well to that time and then the buildup. Like, he's never really been shut down."
The Red Sox are 9-10 in their past 19 games following a 32-5 stretch that included a 15-game winning streak. Boston has not scored since Jarren Duran hit a grand slam in the 11th inning of Tuesday's 7-3 win over the host Miami Marlins.
Rafaela had two hits Friday but was doubled off first base once and later thrown out at home plate in a game in which the Red Sox had six walks, went 1-for-7 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10.
"We just didn't probably execute when we needed to," Rafaela said after Boston was blanked in consecutive games for the first time this season. "I made some dumb decisions. We come back tomorrow, and win two and win the other one, we win the series. That's the plan - win the series and go home."
Rookie left-hander Jake Bennett (8-6, 3.49), who limited the Yankees to one run on three hits in 6 1/3 innings June 27 while opposing Cole, starts the opener. Since facing New York, Bennett is 6-3 with a 4.61 ERA in his past nine starts and earned the win when he allowed four runs in seven innings against San Francisco on Sunday.
The Red Sox did not announce their pitching plans for the second game and may use an opener followed by Brayan Bello as a bulk reliever.
--Field Level Media

Wall Street piles on rate-hike bets as Fed chair Warsh renews hawkish tone

The dollar rallied and gold fell, while 30-year Treasury yields were little changed, signaling confidence that the Fed will act to contain inflation and keep long-term borrowing costs in check.

Ye Xie
,  Michael MacKenzie
 and  Greg Ritchie

29 August, 2026 04:21 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Traders work on the floor of the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US. | Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

For one day at least, bond traders got the message they were waiting for as Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh doubled down on his vow to finally tame inflation that’s outpaced the central bank’s target for five straight years.

The tone of his Jackson Hole, Wyoming, speech wasn’t new. But it was enough to dispel some of the doubts about the new Fed chief that this month helped drive long-dated Treasury yields to a nearly two decade high, pull down the US dollar and send investors rushing for rival havens like gold or Bitcoin.

After Warsh spoke, two-year Treasury yields shot up by 12 basis points to 4.35%, the biggest jump since he struck a similarly hardline posture toward inflation in his first post-meeting press conference in June.

Traders piled into bets that a quarter-point rate hike next month is more likely than not. The dollar rallied, gold dropped and 30-year yields were little changed — all signals that the Fed will act to cool inflation over time and, in so doing, keep long-term borrowing costs under control.

Show Full Article

“He came into this speech at Jackson Hole with the intention of rebuilding that credibility,” said Brian Quigley, who heads the US Treasuries team at Vanguard Group Inc. “You look at the market reaction, I think that was very effective.”

Alongside Nvidia Corp.’s earnings, Warsh’s appearance at the annual symposium was this week’s tone-setting event for global markets.

Yields had been steadily heading up ever since the US war on Iran hit the global economy with an energy-price shock earlier this year and the Fed continued to stick with its wait-and-see stance. But after 30-year yields hit the highest levels since 2007, that started raising renewed concerns and exerting a drag on stock prices in the wake of the recent record-setting run.

Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent made an unusual effort to stop yields from rising by announcing plans to buy back more bonds, which fanned fears that Washington was looking to artificially cap longer-term rates without addressing the inflation and yawning budget deficit that have been pushing them higher.

Warsh also contributed to the market’s selloff. When the Fed held rates steady again in July — despite his hawkish tone a month earlier — long-term bond yields jumped sharply as traders demanded higher payouts in return for the risk of heightened inflation. Some of his comments, including questioning whether the Fed’s preferred price gauge remains the right target, added to doubts about his commitment to price stability.

On Friday, he moved to allay those worries. He made no effort to downplay the inflation figures this week that showed it was running at 3.7%, saying underlying trends haven’t “meaningfully improved.” He said he considers the Fed’s 2% target as “firm and fixed.” And while he has broken from his predecessors’ practice of providing guidance on where rates are heading, he said the Fed needs to ensure that inflation is receeding back to that level “at sufficient speed.”

After his remarks, traders boosted the odds of rate hikes, with swaps showing traders see a more than 50% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Sept. 16 meeting. At least one such move by the end of the year is seen as virtually assured, with two now seen as a strong possibility.

Economists at Barclays changed their Fed calls on Friday, expecting a quarter-point hike in September followed by another increase at the December meeting. The bank previously predicted no increases this year.

“Call it what you want, but this is the exact forward guidance the market was looking for at the July FOMC meeting,” said George Catrambone, head of fixed income at DWS Americas. “He’s going far beyond what was expected, dismissing wage inflation and claiming policy isn’t really restrictive. It’s a pretty big 180 degree turnaround.”

The comments surprised some who had expected an uneventful speech, given that Warsh has been eager not to telegraph the Fed’s next moves. Options based on 10-year note futures had been pricing in a muted market reaction, in a departure from positioning around the Jackson Hole gathering in recent years.

Instead, the jump in two-year Treasury yields was the biggest seen during the event since at least 2010. That rippled across markets, dragging down rate-sensitive tech stocks and Bitcoin, which had benefitted from a revival of the so-called Debasement Trade betting on a weaker US currency.

“What Warsh is adding back is volatility,” said Byron Anderson, head of fixed income at Laffer Tengler Investments, regarding his communications style. “Markets are flip-flopping to every single meeting of his.”

While his remarks were seen as a clear sign that the Fed will start raising rates again, that won’t alone ease bond market pressure that has rippled through to the cost of mortgages and all other types of loans.

What Bloomberg Strategists say…

“An economy at full employment, with inflation above target and not improving quickly, and a rising need for capital arguably requires higher interest rates for the Fed achieve its goal. It’s small wonder that that’s what the market has moved to price.”

—Cameron Crise, Macro Strategist, Markets Live. For the full analysis, click here

The federal government’s nearly $2 trillion annual deficit and the artificial-intelligence investment boom have also played a role by taxing the market’s ability to absorb a flood of new debt. With few signs of a negotiated end to the Iran war in sight, elevated oil prices are also adding to the uncertainty about the outlook.

Moreover, the rapid repricing in markets raises the risk of another potential reversal, like the one after last month’s Fed meeting, if the central bank keeps holding steady and traders are again forced to recalibrate Warsh’s views.

“Let’s see how we settle,” said George Goncalves, head of US macro strategy at MUFG. “If the talk remains tough but tightening is skipped at upcoming meetings, then it’s more of the same.”

items.title: Niger-Des soldats mutins attaquent l'aéroport de Niamey et le palais présidentiel
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Des soldats mutins au Niger ont attaqué samedi dans la matinée l'aéroport et la présidence à Niamey, la capitale du pays, déclenchant une riposte des forces loyalistes, alors que des tirs nourris et des explosions ont été entendus, tandis que la télévision et la radio d'État ont été brièvement mises hors service.
items.body:
Des soldats mutins au Niger ont attaqué samedi dans la matinée l'aéroport et la présidence à Niamey, la capitale du pays, déclenchant une riposte des forces loyalistes, alors que des tirs nourris et des explosions ont été entendus, tandis que la télévision et la radio d'État ont été brièvement mises hors service.
En fin de matinée, le ministère de la Défense du Niger a déclaré que les forces armées reprenaient progressivement le contrôle des sites ciblés, mais des sources sécuritaires ont indiqué que des mutins étaient toujours présents à l'aéroport et que la situation générale restait floue.
La télévision et la radio d'État ont été mis hors service à 8 heures du matin, heure locale (8 heures GMT), avant de reprendre par la suite ses programmes.
La télévision d'État a notamment diffusé un message indiquant que des soldats mutins d'une base de Niamey avaient ouvert le feu sur des "sites sensibles" dans la ville.
Les forces de sécurité ont réagi rapidement et "maîtrisé les troubles", a-t-elle indiqué.
C'est la troisième fois depuis le début de l'année que Niamey - et plus précisément le complexe abritant l'aéroport international et une base aérienne militaire – enregistre d'importants troubles.
Un climat d'insécurité demeure au Niger depuis la prise du pouvoir par les militaires à la suite d'un coup d'Etat survenu en 2023 qui a porté le général Abdourahamane Tiani à la tête du pays. Ce dernier s'était engagé à améliorer la sécurité dans ce pays du Sahel, important producteur d'uranium, mais les attaques djihadistes persistent. En début d'année, des groupes affiliés à Al Qaïda et à l'Etat islamique ont ainsi mené des attaques contre l'aéroport civil et la base aérienne militaire attenante.
L'assaut de samedi a duré des heures et impliqué des soldats des localités d'Ouallam, de Tera et de Dosso, dans le sud-ouest du pays, ont déclaré à Reuters une source sécuritaire nigérienne, ainsi qu'Yvan Guichaoua, chercheur au Centre international d'études des conflits de Bonn.
Les troupes déployées dans cette zone ont subi de lourdes pertes lors des combats contre la branche régionale de l'Etat islamique.
UNE "ATTAQUE LÂCHE", DÉNONCE UN RESPONSABLE NIGÉRIEN Une autre source sécuritaire avait dans un premier temps rapporté à Reuters que des "terroristes" avaient attaqué l'aéroport international Diori Hamani et tenté de pénétrer au-delà du périmètre de sécurité entourant le palais présidentiel.
Un journaliste de Reuters avait également rapporté avoir entendu des tirs nourris aux abords de la présidence aux premières heures de l'aube.
À 9h00 GMT, le palais présidentiel semblait avoir été sécurisé par les troupes loyalistes, mais la zone autour de l'aéroport était toujours contestée, ont indiqué deux sources sécuritaires et un diplomate.
Deux sources ont indiqué que des troupes loyalistes avaient été dépêchées pour reprendre le contrôle de l'aéroport, soit par la négociation, soit par la force.
Selon des analystes et des sources sécuritaires, la frustration envers le gouvernement monte au sein des unités de première ligne.
Bana Wagana Ibrahim, membre du Bureau du Niger au sein du Conseil consultatif et député au Parlement de l'Alliance des Etats du Sahel (AES), a déclaré sur Facebook que la Base 101, une importante installation militaire à Niamey, avait été prise pour cible, ajoutant que les forces de sécurité avait repris le contrôle.
"Une autre attaque lâche contre la base 101 et encore une fois nos forces de défense et de sécurité ont assuré(...) Situation sous contrôle", a-t-il écrit.
Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier ces informations de manière indépendante.
Un porte-parole du gouvernement nigérien n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaires.
LE NIGER, PRODUCTEUR CLÉ D'URANIUM Le Niger, pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest riche en minéraux et possédant d'importantes ressources en uranium, en pétrole et en or, est dirigé par des militaires depuis le coup d'État de juillet 2023 qui a renversé le président Mohamed Bazoum.
Comme ses voisins le Mali et le Burkina Faso, le Niger fait face à une insurrection armée de groupes djihadistes liés à Al Qaïda et l'Etat islamique et n'est jusqu'ici pas parvenu à inverser la tendance, malgré les promesses des dirigeants militaires d'améliorer la sécurité.
La branche ouest-africaine d'Al Qaïda a revendiqué l'attentat perpétré en juin contre l'aéroport de Niamey, cinq mois après que l'Etat islamique au Sahel a ciblé le même site.
Le gouvernement d'Abdourahamane Tiani a décidé de tourner le dos aux partenaires occidentaux traditionnels du Niger et d'approfondir ses liens avec la Russie. Il a également rompu ses liens avec le bloc régional de la CEDEAO pour rejoindre le Mali et le Burkina Faso afin de former un bloc dissident.
Ces troubles surviennent alors que les autorités nigériennes renforcent leur contrôle sur le secteur de l'uranium, après avoir saisi des actifs du groupe français Orano. Le Niger est un fournisseur clé de combustible nucléaire pour l'Europe, représentant environ 15% de l'approvisionnement en uranium d'Orano à pleine capacité.
La semaine dernière, le gouvernement a réattribué les anciens permis d'exploitation d'uranium d'Orano et de GoviEx à des entreprises soutenues par l'Etat, conformément à un décret.

items.title: Une frappe russe sur un entrepôt près de Kyiv provoque une explosion, faisant 37 morts
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Une frappe aérienne russe sur un entrepôt dans la région de Kyiv, survenue dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi, a provoqué une explosion et fait au moins 37 morts, ont indiqué samedi les autorités ukrainiennes.
items.body:
Une frappe aérienne russe sur un entrepôt dans la région de Kyiv, survenue dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi, a provoqué une explosion et fait au moins 37 morts, ont indiqué samedi les autorités ukrainiennes.
Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky à demander des comptes après cette explosion survenue dans un entrepôt, dont le bilan est l'un des plus lourds de ces derniers mois et qui semble être le deuxième incident de ce type en deux mois.
"Ceux qui ont laissé cela se produire doivent répondre de leurs décisions", a-t-il écrit sur le réseau social X, ajoutant que des poursuites pénales avaient déjà été ouvertes pour négligence officielle.
"La réglementation est en vigueur : les munitions ne peuvent être stockées à proximité des habitations ou d'autres zones résidentielles. Les conclusions qui s'imposent seront certainement tirées", a-t-il ajouté.
Des dizaines de personnes ont été blessées et plus de 370 personnes ont été évacuées de la zone de la frappe dans le village de Myla, a déploré le chef de l'Etat ukrainien.
Les infrastructures avoisinantes ont subi des "dégâts importants", a-t-il ajouté, notamment des bâtiments résidentiels et un établissement de soins pour personnes âgées.
La Russie a intensifié son offensive aérienne contre l'Ukraine, utilisant davantage de missiles balistiques et de drones à réaction difficiles à abattre.
Neuf autres régions ukrainiennes ont été visées par des frappes nocturnes menées par la Russie, selon Volodimir Zelensky, notant que la capitale est soumise à des attaques "quasi ininterrompues" de drones à grande vitesse.
Des sirènes ont retenti toute la matinée, pour le troisième jour consécutif, l'armée de l'air ukrainienne mettant en garde contre de nouvelles vagues de drones approchant de la capitale.
Le chef de l'administration de la région de Kyiv, Tymur Tkachenko, a déclaré qu'une jeune fille de 14 ans avait été tuée samedi lors d'une frappe de drones dans le district de Boryspil. A Kyiv, une fillette de deux ans a été tuée par un drone abattu, a dit pour sa part samedi le maire de la ville, Vitali Klitschko.
Les frappes survenues jeudi et vendredi à Kyiv et dans ses environs ont endommagé des entrepôts et des habitations. Certains responsables ukrainiens présentent cette offensive russe comme une campagne visant à "paralyser" la ville.
La récente explosion fait suite à un incident similaire survenu le mois dernier à Vyshneve, une ville de la région de Kyiv, où 10 personnes avaient été tuées et des centaines de maisons endommagées après qu'une frappe a déclenché des explosions secondaires.
"En cette cinquième année de guerre totale, nous n'avons pas le droit de permettre la répétition de tragédies comme celle qui s'est produite à Vyshneve, et celle survenue dans le district de Boutcha", a écrit sur Telegram le Premier ministre Sergii Koretskyi, qui s'est rendu sur le lieu de l'explosion de vendredi.

items.title: Allianz envisage de racheter le géant de l'assistance routière AA pour £5 mds -Sky News
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: L'assureur allemand Allianz envisage de racheter AA, géant britannique de l'assistance routière, pour un montant de 5 milliards de livres sterling (5,84 milliards d'euros), rapporte samedi Sky News.
items.body:
L'assureur allemand Allianz (ALVG.DE) envisage de racheter AA, géant britannique de l'assistance routière, pour un montant de 5 milliards de livres sterling (5,84 milliards d'euros), rapporte samedi Sky News.
Fondé en 1905 par un groupe de passionnés d'automobile et connue en Grande-Bretagne pour ses dépanneuses de couleur jaune, AA a été introduit en Bourse par ses anciens propriétaires, des fonds d'investissement privés, en 2014, au prix de 250 pence par action, avant d'être retiré de la cote.
Allianz fait partie des rares prétendants, aux côtés de la société de capital-investissement EQT, a avoir engagé des discussions avec les conseillers d'AA en vue d'un éventuel un accord, a indiqué Sky News.
Les propriétaires d'AA ont étudié depuis le début de l'année deux options pour le groupe, dont une introduction en Bourse à Londres, a précisé la chaîne de télévision.
Sollicités, Allianz et AA ont refusé de s'exprimer.
Le Financial Times avait rapporté l'année dernière qu'AA envisageait une cession pour 5 milliards de livres sterling et recherchait des acquéreurs.

items.title: The CBSA classified this business’s golf trolleys as Chinese EVs. Now it’s on the hook for $183K in tariffs
items.author: Alex Arsenych
items.summary: Joseph McLuckie can’t count the number of sleepless nights he has had ever since the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) determined about three months ago that his small business owes more than $180, ...
items.body: Joseph McLuckie can’t count the number of sleepless nights he has had ever since the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) determined about three months ago that his small business owes more than $180,000 in tariffs on a more-than-a-year-old shipment. McLuckie is the managing director and owner of JPSM Golf, a small business based out of Pickering, Ont., that sells electric golf trolleys. These trolleys carry golfers’ bags throughout the course as they play. JPSM Golf has been operational for the last 20 years, starting off in the basement of McLuckie’s home in Leaside before it moved to its 9,000-square-foot storefront. Instead of celebrating his company’s 20th anniversary, McLuckie is agonizing whether he will be able to pay all six of his long-term employees should he have to pay the $182,883.95 the CBSA says he owes. “You wake up in the middle of the night, you have a random thought, and it keeps you awake for a couple of hours, because I know if I had to pay this tomorrow, I’m out of cash,” McLuckie said in an interview with CTV News Toronto. The shipment in question was delivered to JPSM Golf from China in April 2025. It was a 40-foot container filled with 330 Formula remote trolleys, a brand McLuckie’s company designed and developed on their own. McLuckie paid Canada’s standard 6.1 per cent import tariff on the trolleys and paid a little more than $19,000 at the time. Thirteen months later, McLuckie said he received a letter from the CBSA saying they had reviewed his shipment and stated the trolleys have been reclassified under a different tariff, subjecting them to the China Surtax Order. This federal tariff first went into effect in October 2024, hitting a wide range of Chinese-made EVS from passenger cars to delivery vans with a 100 per cent levy that was added on top of the existing Most-Favoured Nation import tariff of 6.1 per cent. Ottawa officially repealed the surtax on March 1, 2026. Trade lawyer hired McLuckie said he called the CBSA to see why he was being charged this tax, perplexed on how this could even be applied to his trolleys. He was instructed to file a submission to the CBSA, which he did with the guidance from a trade and customs lawyer. “The position we took was, ‘Well, first of all, the surtax was intended to assist Canada’s auto industry.’ That means automobiles that are motor vehicles, not things that technically are classified as motor vehicles like golf trolleys,” Greg Kanargelidis, the lawyer JPSM Golf hired, said in an interview. “The challenge is that the tariff classification number quoted on the import documents was the one that’s in the surtax list.” In their submission, JPSM Golf argued its products are properly classified under the tariff code 9506.03, representing other golf equipment or as accessories to golf clubs, and that the CBSA should permit redetermination of its products. The CBSA rejected JPSM Golf’s argument. McLuckie raised his eyebrows at the agency’s response. McLuckie pointed specifically to a section of the letter where the CBSA quoted Merriam-Webster’s dictionary, saying “your product does meet the terms of a vehicle.” In the letter sent from CBSA, reviewed by CTV News Toronto, the agency did refer to Merriam-Webster and Cambridge dictionary definitions to determine the separate meanings of “motor” and “vehicle” as each are not defined in the tariff. The CBSA officer concluded the trolleys employ an electric motor for propulsion and are used to transport golf bags, “undoubtedly” qualifying them as a motor vehicle. If a traditional wheelbarrow can be considered as a vehicle, the CBSA officer noted, so can a golf trolley. Based on previous decisions by the Canadian International Trade Tribunal, the independent quasi-judicial body responsible for appeals of CBSA tariff classification decisions, relying on dictionary definitions is “appropriate” when the terms are unclear in the existing coding system, a CBSA spokesperson told CTV News Toronto. The CBSA otherwise could not comment on JPSM Golf’s case specifically, citing confidential customs information. With regards to surtaxes, the enforcement agency said the CBSA makes their decisions based on the “legal wording of individual surtax orders.” “While the Agency does not have the authority to deviate from the wording of a surtax order in its administration, under section 115 of the Customs Tariff, the Minister of Finance has the authority to recommend remission to the Governor in Council,” the CBSA’s statement reads. These remission orders provide full or partial relief from federal tax. Kanargelidis says the remission could amend the China Surtax Order to exclude items like golf trolleys or, if there’s a remission order already in place, it could be amended to add as another item where the surtaxes are remitted to include these products. He says they requested a remission from the Department of Finance, which could assist JPSM Golf’s case in scrapping exorbitant surtax. “Two ways to be successful here is to change the surtax order or to demonstrate that the tariff classification was incorrect to begin with,” Kanargelidis said. The Canadian Federation of Independent Business (CFIB) and Juanita Nathan, MP for Pickering—Brooklin, confirmed to CTV News they have advocated for JPSM Golf to the federal finance ministry. “It’s basically, what we believe, a misclassification of a product, which is what’s happened here. Like it’s basically saying it’s a Chinese EV when, come on, really,” Corinne Pohlmann, executive vice-president of advocacy for the Canadian Federation of Independent Business (CFIB) said in an interview. More than 100 remission requests A Department of Finance Canada official confirmed to CTV News that it has received more than 180 requests for remissions over goods pertaining to the China Surtax Order since October 2024. The official added that the department is currently reviewing another tranche of more than 30 requests “with a view to advancing a sixth remission order this fall.” The department did not directly comment on JPSM Golf’s remission but noted processing times can vary depending on the complexity of their request. “Each request under the China surtax remission framework is thoroughly assessed on its own merits by the Department of Finance, in consultation with domestic producers, to determine whether the goods are in short supply in the Canadian market, cannot reasonably be sourced from non-Chinese suppliers, and whether other exceptional circumstances exist that adversely affect the Canadian economy,” the official wrote. The whole ordeal, in McLuckie’s view, has turned his company into the “unintended consequence and collateral damage” of an act meant to aid and protect the Canadian automobile sector. “If the purpose is to put a 20-year-old small Canadian business out of business, then they’re doing a great job,” McLuckie said.

items.title: Bezzecchi shatters lap record to beat Marquez brothers to Aragon GP pole
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi became the first rider to crack the one minute and 45 seconds barrier at MotorLand, snatching pole position for the Aragon Grand Prix and ending Marc Marquez's bid for a hat-trick of poles at the circuit on Saturday.
items.body:
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi became the first rider to crack the one minute and 45 seconds barrier at MotorLand, snatching pole position for the Aragon Grand Prix and ending Marc Marquez's bid for a hat-trick of poles at the circuit on Saturday.
The Italian initially set the pace with a time of 1:44.984 before going even faster with another lap record of 1:44.962, leaving Ducati's Marquez unable to match the Aprilia rider's scorching pace.
Marquez, who has won seven MotoGP races at Aragon, will start alongside Bezzecchi on the front row despite a heart-stopping moment while braking on a flying lap. His brother Alex Marquez, of Gresini Racing, completes the front row.
"Well, it was a positive morning overall... Obviously, the qualifying was good fun. I'm happy to be fast and to grab the pole position," Bezzecchi said.
"Now the real job starts... We start in a good place, but Marc and Alex are both super fast in terms of pace with both tyres, so it's going to be a tough fight. But we are enjoying and let's see what we can do."
Reigning world champion Marc Marquez accepted that Bezzecchi had the faster bike.
"Marco, at the moment, has a better pace than us, so sometimes you cannot do anything. You just try to do your best and it's what we are doing," he said.
"I pushed hard on that brake point, maybe too much and I had that moment. I feel that I can keep a constant pace, but Marco basically has a bit faster pace."
Trackhouse Racing's Raul Fernandez was fourth-fastest and he will line up on the second row with Aprilia's Jorge Martin and KTM's Pedro Acosta.
The third row features VR46 Racing's Fabio Di Giannantonio, Ducati's Francesco Bagnaia and LCR Honda's Johann Zarco, who made a memorable return from a knee injury sustained in a crash at the Catalan Grand Prix in May.

items.title: Bear encounters are on the rise. Here's what to do if you meet one
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: If it makes contact, play dead, protecting your head, until it goes away.
items.body:
A drought in the western U.S. has devastated wildlands, dried up food sources and sent bears [USN:L6N44M0OO TEXT:"wandering along city sidewalks and into homes and shops"] in search of food.
What should you do if you meet a bear? Reuters turned to BearWise , which bear biologists started in the southeastern United States in 2018 and that grew into a national program of the Association of Fish & Wildlife Agencies.
SHOULD PEOPLE FEAR BEARS? Over millennia, humans have mythologized, vilified and attributed personalities to bears. Smart, strong and fast, bears can weigh hundreds of pounds and are feared predators in the wild. But they typically avoid people and rarely attack them, scientists say.
HOW CAN YOU TELL IF A BEAR FEELS THREATENED? A bear that is huffing, moaning or clacking its jaws is showing it is feeling threatened and prepared to defend itself. BearWise advises standing your ground in the face of a defensive bear, even if it moves toward you. If it makes contact, play dead, protecting your head, until it goes away.
WHAT IF THE BEAR IS AGGRESSIVE? While a defensive bear is noisy and obviously stressed, an aggressive or predatory bear is quiet and moves deliberately. In this situation, experts advise shouting, throwing rocks and using bear spray. If a predatory bear makes physical contact, fight back.
DOES IT MATTER WHETHER IT'S A BLACK OR GRIZZLY BEAR? No, according to Nate Bowersock, a black bear biologist with the Missouri Department of Conservation and chair of the BearWise working group of the Association of Fish & Wildlife Agencies. The key is to respond to the bear's behavior, not its species.
Bears can be hard to tell apart, especially if you are under pressure. Grizzlies, also known as brown bears, are distinguished in appearance by a shoulder hump. Individual black or grizzly bears vary from black to light brown and range in size.
WHERE ARE NORTH AMERICA'S BEARS? Black bears are numerous and found across the U.S. and in Canada and Mexico. Most grizzlies, whose population has rebounded because of conservation efforts, live in Alaska and northern Canada, but also in Montana, Wyoming, Idaho and Washington state.
HOW CAN YOU AVOID TROUBLE? If you spot a bear, do not approach. Do not gather to gawk if a bear shows up in your neighborhood.
If you find a bear in your home or business, leave and call in expert help, Bowersock said.
"Back away quietly," he said.
Do not feed bears, and that includes not leaving pet food outside, keeping trash bins off the street until pickup morning and keeping barbecue grills clean.
IT'S A DROUGHT. SHOULDN'T I FEED THE BEARS? Bowersock said people would be mistaken to think they are helping by feeding bears, and that it is even more important not to do so during a drought.
"If a bear finds food near people and starts to associate human areas with food, they will likely spend even more time in the future near people, even during non-drought times."

items.title: Hungry bears wander into US West homes, shops in record numbers
items.author: Andrew Hay
items.creator: Andrew Hay
items.summary: The driest winter in memory wiped out plants, grasses, berries and nuts that form around 90% of their diet. Their incredible sense of smell is drawing them to human food.
items.body:
Matt Errico was sitting on the toilet when he heard noises in his Colorado home.
The roofer got up and found two young bears about the size of golden retrievers standing in his hallway. After a staring match, they bolted out of the front door.
Errico has had bears get into his garbage before but the home invasion earlier this month was a first.
“I've definitely never heard of bears inside, you know, cubs inside someone's house,” Errico said of bear encounters in his small mountain town of Granby, about 57 miles (92 km) northwest of Denver.
The black bears, also spotted in a Granby vape shop, are among thousands heading into towns and cities across the U.S. West in record numbers.
Bears have wandered near a school in Santa Fe, New Mexico, climbed a tree near a farmers market in Denver and startled humans in other ways across the country after the driest winter in memory wiped out plants, grasses, berries and nuts that form around 90% of their diet, according to bear experts and state wildlife agencies.
The animals' incredible sense of smell is drawing them to human food. That is leading to record bear deaths in some states as hundreds are euthanized, run over, shot and even electrocuted as they interact with humans, according to wildlife agencies.
TESTING THE BEARS With the West's aridification expected to continue, experts fear bears may become habituated to human food and even stop hibernating should winters become too warm and wild food too scarce.
“It's like testing the bears in a way that they've never been tested before, and testing humans,” black bear expert Jon Beckmann said.
Development has moved people into areas where bears used to forage for food. At the same time, bear populations have rebounded in states like Nevada, where they were largely wiped out over a century ago.
Black bears are now the healthiest of the world's eight bear species, with between 17,000 and 20,000 in Colorado alone, according to state authorities.
That state is bearing the brunt of encounters after its human population more than doubled in the last 50 years, pushing homes into bear country around cities like Colorado Springs and Vail.
Colorado, which only has black bears, has had more than 7,000 sightings in 2026, more than the previous full-year record in 2019, according to the state's wildlife agency. There have been at least six bear attacks in the state.
Around 1.5% to 2% of sightings end in euthanization, according to Jonathan Livingston, a spokesperson for Colorado Parks and Wildlife. Bears are typically killed when they are deemed dangerous, such as when they attack humans or break into homes.
Conservation groups like the Colorado Bear Coalition say the animals too often pay with their lives for human negligence, and wildlife agencies should do more to prevent conflicts.
If people alert authorities to bears early, officials can usually avoid euthanizations by scaring off the animals, Livingston added.
Officials and landowners in New Mexico have killed 187 bears this year, the most since 2011, according to the state's wildlife agency, which has relocated 35 adults and 16 cubs. A bear killed a man in New Mexico last week, police reported, marking the state's first fatal attack in 25 years.
Utah authorities said they have euthanized 39 animals in 2026, already a record for any full year.
In Montana, sightings are too numerous to count, with grizzlies moving into areas they have not visited in decades, the state's wildlife agency said. Twenty-four grizzlies have died this year, most killed after attacking livestock or people or being hit by cars, according to the agency, which did not provide historical data. A man was killed by a grizzly in Montana's Glacier National Park in May.
Fatal bear attacks remain rare in the West, with a handful recorded each year.
BEARMAGGEDON? Authorities are calling on residents to use bear-resistant garbage bins, not leave trash containers on the street for days and not put pet food or bird seed within reach of the animals.
Clashes often begin with dumpster diving and can end with a 200- to 400-pound (91-181 kg) black bear, with 3- to 4-inch (8-10 cm) razor-sharp claws, confronting someone in their kitchen, Livingston said.
Nevada bear expert Heather Reich hopes that the animals will find living around humans too stressful and return to the wild, should drought conditions ease. With bears just beginning to put on body weight for hibernation, she fears the encounters will increase.
"We can't even imagine what September and October are going to look like. It is going to be just Armageddon for us," said Reich, a former bear manager for Nevada's wildlife agency who now sells electric doormats to deter bears from entering homes.

items.title: US Open 'RedZone' broadcast hopes to replicate NFL TV success
items.author: Amy Tennery
items.creator: Amy Tennery
items.summary: Tennis fans can keep an eye on 16 courts at once at the year's final Grand Slam as ESPN launches "RedZone at the U.S. Open," a streaming option designed to emulate one of American football's most successful broadcast offerings.
items.body:
Tennis fans can keep an eye on 16 courts at once at the year's final Grand Slam as ESPN launches "RedZone at the U.S. Open," a streaming option designed to emulate one of American football's most successful broadcast offerings.
"RedZone" has been a staple for NFL fans in the U.S. for years, with a multi-hour broadcast shuffling between games to show highlights and live end-zone action without the filler.
Amid a growing U.S. appetite for tennis content, domestic U.S. Open broadcaster ESPN is bringing the concept to Flushing Meadows this year from the opening day of the men's and women's singles main draw on August 30 until September 4.
A dedicated broadcast team will direct coverage from match to match, keeping a close eye on the household names as well as the lesser-known players on the outer courts in New York.
"They'll have access to all 16 courts and all 16 matches that are happening at a given moment," John Suchenski, ESPN's senior director, programming and acquisitions, said. "And they'll make the editorial decisions as to how we move around.
"This is all about what are the most important moments in the matches that are happening right now.
"So going out to Court 13 with two players that are not as recognisable will likely happen because they may be in a very important point of that match," added Suchenski.
"The direction of this offering is to make sure we're getting to the most important point."
The programme comes a year after [USN:L4N3TT1W9 TEXT:"ESPN acquired"] the rights to the "RedZone" brand from the NFL in a deal that placed many of the league's media holdings with the network.
"It obviously will be unique and different and specific to the U.S. Open but we've drawn inspiration from what the NFL has done so well over the years with the NFL RedZone," Suchenski told Reuters, adding that there would be some advertisements included in the broadcast.
The U.S. Open [USN:L2N3OP15C TEXT:"expanded"] in 2025 to an additional day after years of soaring attendances.
ESPN signed a deal with the United States Tennis Association in 2024 to continue broadcasting the tournament until 2037.

items.title: US military families ride 'roller coaster of emotions' over six months of Iran war
items.author: Julia Harte
items.creator: Julia Harte
items.summary: The pressures are familiar for the partners and children, mothers and fathers, of American troops. But the suddenness of the conflict and its fitful pace have had a compounding effect, relatives say.
items.body:
Since the United States went to war with Iran six months ago, Courtney Sanders has been helping soldiers’ families fill the gaps left by their loved ones.
There are school pickups to coordinate, lost incomes to supplement — and the ever-present separation anxiety.
“It's like being on pins and needles all of the time,” Sanders said.
She leads the Chicagoland chapter of Blue Star Families, the nation's largest nonprofit serving military families, and her own daughters are in the U.S. Navy. They have served in various overseas locations over the past six months, including the Middle East.
The U.S. has more than 50,000 troops stationed across the region and has deployed thousands of additional Marines and sailors to support the war effort. Eighteen U.S. service members [USN:L6N44I0PX TEXT:"have been killed"] in the conflict and more than 750 wounded.
During the war's on-and-off fighting, shuttle diplomacy and [USN:L1N44E0F1 TEXT:"failed peace talks"], military families have experienced a “roller coaster of emotions,” Sanders said. “The moment that you feel you're able to take a breath, you get gut-punched again.”
These are familiar pressures for the partners and children, mothers and fathers, of American troops. But the suddenness of the Iranian conflict, and its fitful pace, have had a compounding effect, relatives told Reuters.
In a Blue Star Families poll of some 200 active-duty military families in early March, 81% reported elevated stress from the Iran conflict.
The group has responded by stepping up its programming, creating online resource hubs, hosting webinars and in-person meet-ups, and matching military spouses going through a deployment for the first time with those who have been through it before.
Many service members' deployments have been extended unexpectedly.
The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier went more than 200 days without a [USN:P8N3S5026 TEXT:"port call"] — a modern-day record, according to Democratic lawmakers — and military outlets reported suicide attempts and declining morale among its 5,000 sailors and Marines. U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the reports “completely misrepresented” the conditions on board.
Some military families find themselves in financial straits.
National Guard members, for example, often work regular jobs when they are not deployed. The sudden loss of their main paycheck can make it hard for those left behind to keep food on the table, Sanders said.
"There is a huge misconception in the civilian world that if you are in the military, all of your bills are taken care of,” she said. “And that is just frankly not true.”
In a statement, the Pentagon said: "We see these families (and) we hear their concerns. We will do whatever is necessary to provide the resources, assistance, and stability they need and deserve during these challenging times."
'A LOT OF EMOTIONS' Shannon, an Army spouse and mother of three in North Carolina who requested Reuters use only her first name for security reasons, tries to tune out the news and the political debate surrounding the war.
In February, her husband deployed to the region with five days' notice and could only contact her sporadically for the first several months.
Although they have maintained near-daily communication since June, "there are a lot of emotions,” Shannon said, “especially when people are dying over there.”
Her children started therapy over the summer. She tries to be strong in front of them, but cries sometimes when they’re not around.
Soon after her husband's deployment, Shannon joined an Army-sponsored soldier-and-family "readiness group" within her husband's unit, helping organize meal trains and other support for family members in need.
"Every day is not going to be a great day, but you've gotta just keep going and keep yourself busy," she said.
In Virginia, Pat, a Navy spouse who also asked to be identified by her first name for security reasons, has tried to keep life as normal as possible for her children, who are in middle and high school.
Since her husband deployed about five months ago, Pat said, her neighbors have been "amazing" about helping with kid pickups and other chores.
Her family wears red on Fridays — a show of support for deployed service members — and so do many of her children's classmates, even those without military connections.
Pat's husband has deployed before. She was pleasantly surprised this time to discover his ship had Wi-Fi, making communication easier.
Still, her family is grappling with the uncertainty of when he will return.
"Having older kids and knowing that dad wasn't there to see those sporting events, some of that's been a little emotional," she said. "But my kids are very resilient."
