items.title: The Week in Breakingviews: When fines are fine
items.author: Liam Proud
items.creator: Liam Proud
items.summary: Meta agreed to pay up to $18 bln to resolve claims that it designed Facebook and Instagram to addict children. This week’s update asks whether legal hits and watchdog fines are too small to work. Plus: Prudential walks a fine line in Hong Kong, and US prison stocks have surged.
items.body:
Welcome back! Liam here, filling in for Peter Thal Larsen. Anthropic’s initial public offering [USN:L4N44O1S2 TEXT:"seems close"]. As you read the listing document, keep in mind some lessons from my colleague Karen Kwok’s coverage. To summarise: the Claude developer’s recent growth deceleration is [USN:L6N44F12H TEXT:"no cause"] for panic; its shares could [USN:L6N42414K TEXT:"serve"] as M&A currency; the risks include [USN:L6N41Y0ZA TEXT:"corporate AI"] fatigue, [USN:L6N42M074 TEXT:"governments"] and [USN:L6N4250T1 TEXT:"open-source"] models; and “run-rate” revenue figures are [USN:L6N3ZY167 TEXT:"misleading"]. More to add? Email me . (If this newsletter was forwarded to you, sign up here to get it in your inbox every weekend.)
OPENING LINE “How do you know when a hedge fund manager is talking his book? His mouth is moving.”
Read more: [USN:L6N44M0TI TEXT:"Beware hedge fund managers trashing US policy"].
FIVE THINGS I LEARNED FROM BREAKINGVIEWS THIS WEEK Alibaba’s AI capex splurge implies a “mid-teens” return on invested capital, Morgan Stanley analysts calculate. ([USN:L6N44L04S TEXT:"Time to deliver"])
U.S. and Canadian cinemas sold $4.4 billion of tickets between May and August 23, about 6% ahead of 2019. ([USN:L6N44L0Q9 TEXT:"Thanks to higher prices"])
Absolut vodka owner Pernod Ricard’s sales fell 19% year-on-year in China in the financial year to June. ([USN:L6N44O0LS TEXT:"Time for a dividend cut"])
Nvidia had struck $70 billion of direct equity investments as of August 17. ([USN:L6N44N16H TEXT:"Plus $230 billion of backstops"])
Unitree and its rival Chinese robot makers may ship 100,000 units this year. ([USN:L6N44O093 TEXT:"But its CEO is not smiling"])
COST OF BUSINESS No CEO wants to be in the position that Mark Zuckerberg found himself in this week. His tech giant Meta Platforms (META.O) on Wednesday [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"agreed"] to pay up to $18 billion to settle claims, made by nearly all U.S. states, that the company designed Facebook and Instagram to keep children addicted to social media.
Still, its shares ended the day up 1%, indicating either that investors didn’t care or perhaps that the sum was smaller than they feared. As Jonathan Guilford [USN:L6N44O06H TEXT:"pointed out"], it’s a tiny amount relative to the roughly $80 billion of net income that analysts expect Meta to generate this year.
The legal payments are also spread over a decade, which means they’re lower in today’s money than the headline figure suggests. For the sake of simplicity, assume 10 equal installments starting immediately and discounted at a 10% rate. The present value would be $12 billion, or 0.8% of Meta’s almost $1.5 trillion market capitalisation.
In India, meanwhile, Shritama Bose [USN:L6N44L0HZ TEXT:"dug into"] a decision by the local regulator to bar a JPMorgan entity and another Mumbai-based broker. It’s part of a [USN:L6N42X0BM TEXT:"wider crackdown"] on what the watchdog sees as market manipulation in the country’s $6 trillion equity derivatives market. The financial penalty in this case? Just a few hundred thousand dollars. That won’t trouble JPMorgan (JPM.N) boss Jamie Dimon much.
True, in both cases the real punishment is arguably non-financial. Zuckerberg, for example, pledged meaningful changes to Meta’s apps, including age verification, limiting 14-to-17-year-olds to two hours of usage and restricting night-time notifications. Yet Jonathan is sceptical that these tweaks will amount to much, [USN:L6N44O06H TEXT:"concluding"] that Meta has ultimately paid a small price to secure its industry status.
More broadly, it’s notable that fines and other similar penalties don’t seem to have kept pace with soaring stock markets in recent years. Good Jobs First, a non-profit that “promotes corporate and government accountability in economic development”, keeps a database that tracks regulatory punishments and other payouts related to corporate misconduct, including many legal cases like those brought by state attorneys general.
Total annual U.S. penalties peaked at $84 billion in 2024, but that figure was not much bigger than the previous high of $81 billion in 2015. For comparison, the total value of the benchmark S&P 500 Index almost tripled over the same period. In other words, the drag to shareholders from corporate misconduct seems to be fading as a percentage of overall market capitalisation.
None of this is to say that Zuckerberg can rest easy. He will have a lot of other things on his mind this weekend. Robert Cyran, drawing on a Reuters investigation , on Wednesday [USN:L6N44M10Z TEXT:"examined"] why Meta’s efforts to remake itself around artificial intelligence have run into repeated setbacks.
The takeaway is striking. Technological revolutions are always tough for incumbents, and Meta is now one of them. That’s a far bigger problem for the company than a legal bill that failed to dent the share price.
CHART OF THE WEEK Beijing has been [USN:L4N42D0HQ TEXT:"tightening"] its [USN:L4N4420RA TEXT:"grip"] on Chinese wealth held outside of the mainland, particularly in [USN:L4N42P0F4 TEXT:"Hong Kong"]. It’s not great news for insurers like [USN:L4N44H0E1 TEXT:"AIA"] and Prudential. Policies bought in the financial centre have long been a popular channel for mainland visitors to diversify their assets offshore. But as Katrina Hamlin [USN:L6N44O007 TEXT:"showed"] in this chart on Thursday, which was published alongside a piece about Prudential’s results, the underlying demand is still strong. And some types of policies seem less vulnerable than others.
THE WEEK IN PODCASTS For a long time, the received wisdom among Western economists was that liberal democracy and capitalism go hand in hand. Today, that consensus lies in tatters. On The Big View , economist Daron Acemoglu tells Peter Thal Larsen that the institutions, laws and freedoms that made the West rich are under threat. The Nobel laureate has a plan to change that.
Over on the Viewsroom , Aimee Donnellan, Jonathan Guilford and Gabriel Rubin previewed Kevin Warsh’s first Jackson Hole symposium as chair of the Federal Reserve. His strategy of staying tight-lipped on interest rates, and hoping investors will focus on the real economy, may have long-term consequences.
PARTING SHOT Of all the so-called Trump trades that rose to prominence at the start of the U.S. president’s second term, prison stocks have been arguably the most enduring. GEO (GEO.N) and CoreCivic (CXW.N) together oversee approximately 165 correctional facilities, with space for roughly 160,000 inmates. As Jeffrey Goldfarb [USN:L6N44A1BM TEXT:"writes"], they’ve trounced the benchmark S&P 500 Index since November 2024, even though violent crime has been falling for years. An enlarged and emboldened Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency is keeping wardens busy, but it doesn’t look politically or financially sustainable.

items.title: Manila like a local
items.author: Karen Lema
items.creator: Karen Lema
items.summary: Our bureau chief’s guide to adobo, jeepneys and streetwear.
items.body:
REUTERS/Illustration/Kate Evans The first things you notice when you arrive in Manila are the traffic, the clinging heat and the constant noise. It can feel overwhelming initially, with streets that rarely seem to slow down.
But stay a little longer, and something else begins to emerge. Manila is not just a city of congestion and chaos. It is also a place of warm welcomes, lively street life and food that draws people together. Beneath the frenetic pace is a city shaped by centuries of history, with neighbourhoods still anchored by Spanish churches and cobblestone streets worn down by time and footsteps, where conversations linger and weekend escapes to beaches and mountains are never far away.
I was born in the Philippines and have spent two decades covering the country for Reuters — its economic cycles, its political upheavals and its navigation of its place in an increasingly tense region. What emerges is a city that can be rough and uneven, yes, but also layered and beautiful.
Here’s how to experience Manila like a local:
The way around: I love to cycle, but Manila often has other ideas. This is not a city known for its bike lanes, and public transport can be patchy and unpredictable. You learn to adapt.
A jeepney drives through Binondo, the world's oldest Chinatown, in Manila, Philippines, August 24, 2026. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez The most iconic transport option is the jeepney, a colourful, open-sided minibus also known as the "King of the Road," and a symbol of Filipino ingenuity. They’re cheap and ubiquitous — fares start at around 14 pesos ($0.22), if you don’t mind the heat and sitting shoulder to shoulder with strangers.
For more predictable trips, there’s Grab, the ride-hailing app that has become a go-to for many professionals despite the higher cost. The Light Rail Transit and Metro Rail Transit offer a faster way to cut through the traffic , connecting Manila with neighbouring cities in the capital region, though trains can be crowded during peak hours.
Things to see: One of the bestplaces to begin your exploration is Intramuros, the old walled city that served as the seat of Spanish colonial power in the heart of the capital. Its centuries-old churches, stone fortifications and cobblestone streets offer a glimpse into Manila's colonial past.
People walk along Fort Santiago at Intramuros in Manila, Philippines, August 24, 2026. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People sit at Casa Manila in Intramuros, Manila, Philippines, August 24, 2026. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez From there, continue to Binondo, the world’s oldest Chinatown, where commerce hums alongside a wide array of Chinese dishes, noodle shops, dim sum restaurants, and bakeries selling steamed pork buns, sweet bean-filled pastries and spring rolls in a way that feels both ancient and entirely present.
A few streets away stands Quiapo Church , home to the revered "Black Nazarene" statue of Christ, whose annual January procession draws millions of devotees in one of the largest expressions of Catholic faith in Asia. Not far away is Rizal Park, popularly known as Luneta, where the imposing monument to national hero José Rizal — whose writings helped inspire the movement that led to the Philippine Revolution in the 1890s against Spanish rule — stands watch over the city.
An ice cream vendor, locally known as Mamang Sorbetero, prepares a cone of ice cream as a girl looks over the ice cream cart at Quiapo. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A kalesa, or a horse-drawn carriage, waits for passengers, at Intramuros. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People walk past a balut vendor at Binondo, the world's oldest Chinatown. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A jeepney passes by the Rizal Park. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People walk on a street in Manila. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A couple sits by the Manila Bay. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez Beaded rosaries in various colours are displayed for sale outside Quiapo Church at Quiapo. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez

People sit and look at art in the National Museum of Fine Arts. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A kalesa, or a horse-drawn carriage, waits for passengers, as a pedicab passes by at Intramuros. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez Commuters on board the Light Rail Transit (LRT). REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez The Light Rail Transit (LRT) passes by in Manila. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A vendor prepares fruit juice for customers at Binondo, the world's oldest Chinatown. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez Catholic figurines are displayed for sale outside Quiapo Church at Quiap. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A woman takes a photo at Manila Bay. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People sit at Plazuela de Santa Isabel, where the Manila 1945 Memorial is situated, in Intramuros. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People take a selfie outside the Minor Basilica and National Shrine of Jesus Nazareno, commonly known as Quiapo Church, at Quiapo. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People enjoy at Papakape, a cafe at the National Museum of Fine Arts. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A passenger rides on the rear of a jeepney. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A woman stands outside a cafe at Intramuros. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People sit at Plaza de Roma at Intramuros. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People walk at Binondo, the world's oldest Chinatown. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A fruit vendor sits on a sidewalk at Binondo, the world's oldest Chinatown. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez People buy fish balls, a popular street food, at Binondo, the world's oldest Chinatown. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez A couple poses for a photo with Juan Luna's Spoliarium in the background at the National Museum of Fine Arts. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez Across the park lies the National Museum Complex , home to archaeological treasures, ethnographic collections and some of the country's most important works of art, including Juan Luna's "Spoliarium," a monumental 19th-century painting depicting fallen gladiators being dragged from a Roman arena. A couple of kilometres away, overlooking the Pasig River, you'll find Malacañang Palace, the official residence and workplace of the Philippine president, originally built during the Spanish colonial era.
For a glimpse of Manila at its most frenetic, head to Divisoria, a sprawling wholesale and retail market packed with malls, street stalls and warehouses. Here, shoppers weave through crowds in search of bargains on everything from clothes and shoes to party supplies, decorations, household goods and gadgets, with goods including low-cost imports and locally made products.
The definitive food item: If you’ve spent any time on food shows or travel blogs, you’ve likely come across adobo, the Philippines’ most recognisable dish. At its simplest, it is pork or chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, peppercorns and bay leaves, creating a balance of sour and savoury flavours. It is also forgiving: even someone like me, who rarely cooks, can make a decent adobo. For a restaurant version, many locals swear by Manam 's.
Adobo, a Filipino dish of pork and chicken cooked in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, peppercorns and bay leaves, is served at a branch of Manam restaurant; Balut, a fertilised duck egg with a partially developed embryo, is displayed for sale at a street food cart at Binondo; Vinegar is poured on a plastic cup of duck eggs, locally known as penoy, at a street food stall at Divisoria. REUTERS/Eloisa Lopez Then there is balut, a fertilised duck egg with a partially developed embryo, often eaten straight from the shell on the street. It has appeared on TV shows like “Fear Factor” because of how it looks, but locals see it as a protein-rich snack, best enjoyed warm with salt or vinegar.
Even outsiders might be familiar with Jollibee, the homegrown fast-food giant where crispy Chickenjoy, sweet-style spaghetti and peach mango pie have become comfort-food staples across generations.
To wash it down, there is fresh coconut juice sold on street corners, scooped straight from the shell and served over ice, with tender coconut meat included. For runners like me, it is the perfect recovery drink.
For dessert, try halo-halo, which literally means “mix-mix,” a concoction of sweetened beans, jellies and fruit layered beneath shaved ice, milk, caramel custard and purple yam. My personal favourite is found at Razon's , whose pared-down version proves that less can sometimes be more. Others recommend Bebang's , which uses frozen milk instead of shaved ice.
Beneath the frenetic pace is a city shaped by centuries of history, with neighbourhoods still anchored by Spanish churches and cobblestone streets worn down by time and footsteps, where conversations linger and weekend escapes to beaches and mountains are never far away.
Dress like a local: In Manila’s heat and humidity, breathable fabrics are essential. Cotton remains a reliable choice and on any given day you will see cotton shirts paired with shorts or loose trousers, although many locals have also embraced modern technical textiles. Local brands BENCH/ and Penshoppe are everywhere, offering affordable everyday clothing. Footwear tends toward the practical — I usually opt for sneakers, which are best for Manila’s uneven sidewalks.
If you really want to fit in, carry an umbrella — useful as much for shade as for the sudden downpours.
Getting away: A two- or three-hour drive out of the city takes you to beaches, mountains and cooler air.
In Batangas, 66 miles (107 km) south of Manila, the water clears and the pace slows. Diving spots around Anilao attract everyone from beginners to seasoned divers for their vibrant coral reefs and sea turtles. One of its best-known sites is The Cathedral, which features an underwater cross surrounded by reef fish.
Or head to Tagaytay, perched on a ridge overlooking Taal Volcano — one of the world’s smallest active volcanoes, which sits on an island in the middle of a lake. The city has become a food destination, known for bulalo, a rich beef marrow soup, tawilis, a freshwater sardine found only in Taal Lake, and buko (coconut) pie, a regional staple. Cafes make the most of the breeze.
For something more active, hike up Mount Makiling, a volcano steeped in folklore, or ride the rapids at Pagsanjan Falls.
CITY MEMO DATA POINTS
Population: 1.9 million
Price of a cup of coffee: 15 pesos ($0.24) for a black coffee from a roadside stall, poured from a thermos. For something a step up but distinctly Filipino, head to Bo’s Coffee , which champions local beans, or Figaro , a long-time fixture of the café scene. Newer chains such as But First, Coffee reflect how quickly Manila’s coffee culture is evolving, with most drinks costing less than 300 pesos ($4.50).
Price of an ice cream scoop: 10-20 pesos ($0.16-0.32) for a scoop from roaming ice cream vendors pushing colourful carts and referred to as Mamang Sorbetero. The name comes from sorbetes, a traditional Filipino frozen dessert, and “mamang,” a familiar way of referring to an older man. They sell coconut-based ice cream, churned the old-fashioned way and served in flavours such as cheese, chocolate, ube and mango. For something more artisan, Manila Creamery offers Filipino-inspired flavours such as ube, tablea and durian for 120-160 pesos ($1.95-$2.60) per scoop.
Great place to see a sunset: Manila Bay — sitting at a café on Roxas Boulevard, walking the bay front, or looking out from a hotel balcony.
Oldest university: University of Santo Tomas, founded in 1611 and now home to more than 40,000 students.

items.title: Chopra ends season early after ligament tear
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Former Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra has ended his 2026 season early after sustaining a ligament tear during training, the javelin thrower announced in an Instagram post on Saturday, three weeks before the Asian Games.
items.body:
Former Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra has ended his 2026 season early after sustaining a ligament tear during training, the javelin thrower announced in an Instagram post on Saturday, three weeks before the Asian Games.
The 28-year-old Indian, who took gold at the Tokyo Olympics and won silver in Paris, placed second in the Lausanne Diamond League with a throw of 88.05 metres last week, but suffered the injury soon after, getting sidelined for a long period for the second time in a year.
"After discussions with my doctor and team, we've decided that I will sit out the rest of this season," Chopra posted.
"It's disappointing, especially because I felt close to finding my rhythm. But as they say, setbacks are a part of the journey."
Chopra, who was dealing with lower back discomfort since 2023, aggravated a disc injury in September 2025 during training. He went into a nine-month rehabilitation period after the Tokyo World Championships, and returned in June.
He had qualified for the Diamond League finals next week, and was a medal hope for India at next month's Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
"My focus now is on recovering well and coming back even stronger," Chopra added.

items.title: Russian strike on Kyiv-area ammunition depot triggers blast, killing 37
items.author: Dan Peleschuk
items.creator: Dan Peleschuk
items.summary: At least 37 people were killed after a Russian drone attack on a Kyiv-area ammunition depot sparked a detonation, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Saturday, vowing to punish suspected negligence in the second such incident in two months.
items.body:
At least 37 people were killed after a Russian drone attack on a Kyiv-area ammunition depot sparked a detonation, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Saturday, vowing to punish suspected negligence in the second such incident in two months.
The deadliest Russian strike in the Kyiv area this year came as Moscow's air attacks on the Ukrainian capital and surrounding region dragged into a third straight day, killing residents, damaging homes and derailing daily life.
Dozens were also injured and hundreds evacuated from the area of the strike late on Friday on the village of Myla, Zelenskiy said, where nearby infrastructure including residential buildings and a facility for the elderly and people with disabilities suffered "significant damage".
The attack sparked widespread fires, officials said. Among those killed was the head of a neighbouring village who rushed to help.
"A terrible situation and terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosives right next to people," Zelenskiy said in a video address.
SECOND STRIKE-RELATED DETONATION IN TWO MONTHS The site of Friday's blast was a military facility that held artillery shells, mines and drones, among other ammunition, he added.
It followed [USN:L1N43705J TEXT:"a similar incident"] in the Kyiv-area town of Vyshneve last month, when 10 people were killed and hundreds of houses damaged after a strike triggered secondary explosions.
"Another such crime – after what happened in Vyshneve – is absolutely unacceptable," Zelenskiy said. "I expect the details to be presented to the public promptly."
He added that criminal cases had already been opened on charges of official negligence. Ukrainian officials rarely disclose damage to military targets from Russian attacks.
In a statement on Saturday, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said all those responsible for weapons storage should complete a full audit of their locations.
DRONE SWARMS GRIP KYIV FOR DAYS Nine other regions had been targeted in overnight strikes by Russia, Zelenskiy added, saying Kyiv in particular was under "virtually non-stop attack" from jet-powered drones.
Russia has [USN:L8N42A0SA TEXT:"escalated its air war"] on Ukraine with increasing numbers of elusive ballistic missiles and new high-speed drones, which Kyiv lacks the air defences to shoot down.
On Saturday, sirens blared throughout the morning and afternoon for a third straight day as Ukraine's air force warned of new waves of drones approaching the capital.
The sound of air defences boomed across the sky.
Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko said a 14-year-old girl was killed in a morning drone strike on the Boryspil district. In Kyiv, a 2-year-old girl was killed by a downed drone, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Saturday.
Strikes in and around the city on Thursday and Friday had damaged residential buildings and storage facilities belonging to major retailers, part of what some Ukrainian officials said was [USN:L1N44P057 TEXT:"a campaign aimed at"] "paralysing" the city of several million.

items.title: German insurer Allianz weighs $6.77 billion takeover of AA roadside rescue giant, Sky News reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Germany-based financial services company Allianz is considering a £5 billion ($6.77 billion) takeover swoop for AA, the breakdown recovery group, Sky News reported on Saturday.
items.body:
Germany-based financial services company Allianz (ALVG.DE) is considering a £5 billion ($6.77 billion) takeover swoop for AA, the breakdown recovery group, Sky News reported on Saturday.
AA, founded by a group of motoring enthusiasts in 1905 and known in Britain for its yellow recovery vehicles, was taken public by its previous private equity owners in 2014 at 250 pence a share.
Allianz is one of a small number of parties which have been holding talks with advisers to the AA about a deal, Sky News said, adding that private equity firm EQT was another bidder.
The AA's private equity owners have been pursuing a so-called dual-track process for most of this year, with the alternative to a sale being a public listing on the London Stock Exchange, Sky News said.
Both companies declined to comment.
The Financial Times reported last year that the British roadside recovery company was eyeing a £5 billion sale and was seeking buyers.
($1 = 0.7390 pounds)

items.title: Norris extends to 2030 and would be happy to end career at McLaren
items.author: Alan Baldwin
items.creator: Alan Baldwin
items.summary: Formula One world champion Lando Norris announced a contract extension with McLaren until at least the end of 2030 on Saturday, and said he would be happy to see out his career with a team that felt like home.
items.body:
Formula One world champion Lando Norris announced a contract extension with McLaren until at least the end of 2030 on Saturday, and said he would be happy to see out his career with a team that felt like home.
The 26-year-old Briton, winner of the last two races in Hungary and the Netherlands, broke the news to McLaren employees at a friends and family day at the Woking factory.
McLaren said there was also a multi-year option to commit beyond 2030, and Norris had been gifted an MCL39 car from last season when he became the team's first drivers' champion since Lewis Hamilton in 2008.
Speaking earlier to reporters, Norris said the deal came at a perfect time for team morale and motivation, but the figures seen in some media speculation were wide of the mark.
"At the minute there's really no reason to want to even put a thought into somewhere else," he said. "I kind of want my whole career to be with McLaren because I'm happy here and I don't want to change.
"I want to fight with McLaren even when things are not going well and I want to win with McLaren when things are going amazingly well. So yeah, I'll be very, very happy at the end of my career to say that McLaren was the only team I've been with."
Norris made his McLaren F1 debut in 2019, after joining in 2017 as a test and simulator driver, and has now won 13 grands prix with the reigning constructors' champions, as well as 18 poles.
"This extension gives us important continuity and reinforces our confidence in the direction we are taking together," said team principal Andrea Stella. "With him and Oscar (Piastri), we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula One.”
MORE MONEY BUT NOT AS MUCH AS VERSTAPPEN AND HAMILTON Some media reports have suggested the new deal would put the Briton third in Formula One's pay rankings, behind only Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Hamilton.
One speculated that Norris's new salary could be around €60 million ($69.6 million) a year.
"I feel like I should earn as much as that," he grinned in response to a mention of what four-time champion Verstappen and seven-time champion Hamilton might be on.
"But it's certainly not close to the figures that I've been seeing online, sadly... of course it's a bit more, as it is with any job when you kind of extend and do those things, but it's certainly not close to the level of Lewis or Max, which in a way it shouldn't be, because I've not achieved as much as what they've achieved in their careers.
"I'm working on it, you know. I don't know when my next extension or renewal would be and hopefully I can then try and match it one day. I dream of seeing those figures that I've seen online so I'll keep dreaming of them one day."
Norris said there had been some interest from other teams, but none expressed towards them, and it would have felt like a betrayal to go anywhere else.
"Really it was quite the easiest decision I've had to make in my career so far," he said.

"I'm working on it, you know. I don't know when my next extension or renewal would be and hopefully I can then try and match it one day. I dream of seeing those figures that I've seen online so I'll keep dreaming of them one day."
Norris said there had been some interest from other teams, but none expressed towards them, and it would have felt like a betrayal to go anywhere else.
"Really it was quite the easiest decision I've had to make in my career so far," he said.

items.title: Risk of Lake Burst Near China-Nepal Border Disaster Site Wanes
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The threat of a lake formed after a glacier collapse bursting near the China-Nepal border where a devastating flood occurred earlier this week has decreased, Chinese authorities said on Saturday, as its size appears to have shrunk. Satellite images from Thursday to Saturday morning suggest that …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
The threat of a lake formed after a glacier collapse bursting near the China-Nepal border where a devastating flood occurred earlier this week has decreased, Chinese authorities said on Saturday, as its size appears to have shrunk.

Satellite images from Thursday to Saturday morning suggest that water in the lake – straddling the China-Nepal border at the confluence of two rivers – has been slowly flowing through, decreasing the reservoir gradually, state broadcaster CCTV reported, citing the Water Resources Ministry.

The ministry said satellite imagery of the lake’s surface area on the Purepu Tsangpo river showed it was 99,000 sqm early Saturday morning – about the size of 14 football fields combined – having shrunk by 21,000 sqm compared with images from Thursday.

A glacier collapse on Wednesday, sending a powerful torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris through Himalayan mountain river systems, swept away a border port complex linking China’s Tibet to Nepal, killing hundreds and leaving thousands missing.

Experts and authorities have warned of the extremely high risk of secondary disasters in the valley, especially from the lake formed by glacial debris, which could endanger downstream rescue operations.

State-owned engineering and rescue enterprise China Anneng, which has been monitoring the lake since Thursday, dispatched a 15-member team on Friday, equipped with reconnaissance drones, portable satellite stations, and mobile surveillance cameras, to gather more data about the lake.

An  overflow  from the lake on Friday temporarily halted rescue work before further assessment deemed the risks manageable.

Authorities have also flagged another larger body of water at the bottom of the glacier collapse.

“We estimate its area to be over 120,000 square meters, but its depth is currently unknown,” said Chen Hongqi, a senior engineer at the Ministry of Natural Resources’ Geological Disaster Technical Guidance Center.

Flood risks will  remain  until the two lakes have fully drained, an official with Nepal’s Disaster Management Authority has said.

In bleak rainy weather on Saturday morning, more than 50 rescue workers combed through the grey rubble of boulders and mud looking for signs of life and calling out to any survivors, according to CCTV.

The first team of rescuers and a search-and-rescue dog had made their way to the location of the Gyirong border crossing complex on Friday afternoon, which they described as having  nothing left but ruins .

Dangerous conditions at the main disaster zone, made more complex as roads and communication were cut off, continue to pose challenges to the Chinese relief efforts, state news agency Xinhua said.

China’s death count from the disaster rose to seven early Saturday, with 554 still missing.

Nearly 500 villagers and construction workers, as well as all 555 tourists from the area, have been evacuated, Xinhua said.

items.title: Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell combine for 68 as Fever trounce Sun
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell each scored 34 points, carrying the Indiana Fever past the Connecticut Sun for a 111-91 runaway on Friday night in Indianapolis.
items.body:
Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell each scored 34 points, carrying the Indiana Fever past the Connecticut Sun for a 111-91 runaway on Friday night in Indianapolis.
Clark, who distributed 12 assists, and Mitchell both shot 12-for-19 from the field. Clark connected on 6 of 12 3-point shots, while Mitchell went 4 of 9 from long distance.
Aliyah Boston provided 14 points for Indiana, which overcame a shoddy opening stretch of the game. Makayla Timpson tacked on 10 points and eight rebounds for the Fever (26-14), who have won seven of their past nine games.
Diamond Miller recorded 19 points while rookie Nell Angloma tallied a season-high 17 points off the bench for Connecticut. Aaliyah Edwards and reserve Hailey Van Lith both added 12 points.
The Sun (10-29) began a three-game road trip with their fourth loss in a five-game stretch. They shot 9-for-28 (32.1%) from 3-point range.
Indiana reached the 100-point mark for the third consecutive game.
The Fever outscored the Sun 21-12 on free throws. Indiana ended up making 39 of 67 shots from the floor (58.2%), while Connecticut made 35 of 76 (46.1%).
Connecticut was within 67-57 in the third quarter before the Fever closed the period on a 9-0 spurt.
After a slow start, the Fever built a 58-43 halftime lead, buoyed by a 39-15 scoring advantage in the second quarter. Clark had 18 points while Mitchell had 17 at the break.
Indiana made one of its first eight attempts from 3-point range but then connected five times on its next seven long-range launches.
The Fever held a 24-12 rebounding edge in the first half.
The Sun built a 28-14 lead in the first quarter behind Miller's 12 points. The Fever scored the last five points of the quarter but made only four of 14 shots from the floor in the period overall.
Indiana won all three regular-season games vs. the Sun this season.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Liverpool finalise agreement to sign PSG's Barcola in deal worth up to £123 million, reports say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Liverpool have finalised an agreement to sign French forward Bradley Barcola from European champions Paris St Germain in a deal worth up to £123 million ($166.43 million), media reports said on Saturday, with the 23-year-old set to become the latest high-profile addition to Andoni Iraola's squad.
items.body:
Liverpool have finalised an agreement to sign French forward Bradley Barcola from European champions Paris St Germain in a deal worth up to £123 million ($166.43 million), media reports said on Saturday, with the 23-year-old set to become the latest high-profile addition to Andoni Iraola's squad.
The 20-times English champions will pay a package worth £106 million, with add-ons potentially rising to £17 million, for Barcola, the BBC said. The Athletic reported that he is set to sign a five-year contract.
Reuters has contacted Liverpool and PSG for comment.
Barcola joined PSG from his boyhood club Olympique Lyonnais in 2023 and went on to enjoy a trophy-laden spell in the French capital, winning back-to-back Champions League titles in 2024-25 and 2025-26, three Ligue 1 crowns and two French Cups, among other honours.
He made 152 appearances across all competitions for PSG, scoring 39 goals and supplying 37 assists.
He had two years remaining on his PSG contract.
Barcola would be the latest addition to [USN:L1N42C0TK TEXT:"new manager Andoni Iraola"]'s squad following the close-season arrivals of Uruguayan defender [USN:L1N4470P0 TEXT:"Ronald Araujo"] on loan, French centre back Jeremy Jacquet and Spanish forward [USN:L4N42Q1LJ TEXT:"Victor Munoz"].
Liverpool's attacking options currently include British record signing [USN:L4N3UJ0YF TEXT:"Alexander Isak"], Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Munoz as the Merseyside club adjusts to life after talisman [USN:L1N40C15L TEXT:"Mohamed Salah"]'s departure. Forward [USN:L1N40Y0UY TEXT:"Hugo Ekitike"] is also sidelined with a long-term injury.
Liverpool host Nottingham Forest later on Saturday.
($1 = 0.7390 pounds)

items.title: How Russia is teaching its children to fight the wars of the future
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: The mandatory classes for teenagers include learning about the main types of armaments including machine guns, anti-tank weapons and hand grenades, as well as general military discipline ...
items.body: Students returning to Russian schools next week will discover a change to their civics courses that puts military training at the heart of the lessons. The mandatory classes for teenagers include learning about the main types of armaments including machine guns, anti-tank weapons and hand grenades, as well as emergency field medicine and general military discipline. While some of the skills were previously taught in limited high school modules, the new version escalates this training for children as young as 13. The revamped curriculum ordered by the Education Ministry requires half of weekly classes in the “Fundamentals of Security and Defense of the Motherland” course to focus on basic military training. It’s part of a creeping militarization of Russia’s schools intended to shape the next generation of army recruits as the Kremlin continues the war in Ukraine that’s now in its fifth year.  “The romanticisation of war and violence, combined with a constant fear of external enemies, instills in young people the idea that human life holds no value and that dying for the regime and the president is normal,” said Pavel Talankin, an exiled Russian teacher who co-directed the Oscar-winning documentary Mr. Nobody Against Putin that focused on rising war propaganda in his school. “If necessary, one must die for the motherland, taking up the flag and marching into the line of fire without asking questions.” As well as instruction on weapons and battlefield tactics, the basic military training covers lessons on Russia’s national security doctrine and the structure of the armed forces. Students will also study mines and explosive hazards, first aid for combat injuries, chemical and radiation exposure and acute stress, as well as survival training and procedures for operating in conflict zones. The educational overhaul effectively helps create a stream of potential recruits from the classroom to the army. It’s backed up by deployment of battlefield veterans from the war in Ukraine into schools and kindergartens to speak to children in support of President Vladimir Putin’s decision to launch the 2022 full-scale invasion. Russia seeks about 400,000 new recruits each year for the war that’s already created more than 1.5 million killed and wounded in the army, according to western estimates.  State Duma speaker Vyacheslav Volodin wants veterans of the war in Ukraine to be placed in “every single school” to teach children in subjects related to their military experience. “Their qualities should be put to use in educating children,” he told university students in Krasnodar in September 2025, pointing to his own Soviet childhood when veterans of World War II were present in schools. In the Soviet Union, basic military training was compulsory in schools including gas mask drills, march practice, and rifle assembly. Communist authorities framed military readiness as a deterrent against foreign aggression so that the catastrophe of the Nazi German invasion in World War II, which cost an estimated 27 million Soviet lives to defeat, would never happen again. “Back then, people feared war, and there was propaganda for peace everywhere, so that war would not happen again,” said Irina Lukyanova, a teacher and researcher who studies trends in Russia’s education system. “But now the ideology is militarism.”    Volodin’s wish is already close to being fulfilled. A survey of more than 2,600 Russian school leaders and teachers conducted by the state-sponsored Knowledge Society (Znanie) found that 95% of schools host events dedicated to the war in Ukraine, more than 80% invite combatants to speak to students, and nearly 75% run special lessons about the war. The classroom pipeline feeds directly into Russia’s conscription system, which requires all 18-year-old men to complete one year’s military service, though in reality many avoid or delay being drafted. While the army can’t send conscripts to Ukraine, enlistment officers and military instructors pressure young draftees to sign lucrative professional contracts early in their training, making them eligible to be sent to fight in the war. Five Ways Putin Is in Trouble Over His War in Ukraine: Explainer Outside the classroom, Russia has revived and modernized Soviet-era youth military games called “Zarnitsa” (Summer Lightning). Organized by the state-backed “Movement of the First” youth group, children are organized into 10-person squads with different military specialties, including commanders, stormtroopers, drone operators, sappers, and medics, undertaking combat simulation training using laser-tag gear, VR flight simulators, trench maneuvers, and assault rifle mockups. Participation in the program has grown from 800,000 children aged from 7 to 17 years in 2024 to an expected 2.5 million this year. The youth organization overseeing the games receives annual funding of about 20 billion rubles ($233 million) from the federal budget. High school boys are also offered week-long barracks-style field training at state-run ‘Avangard’ military centers — a nationwide network spanning over 70 facilities backed by tens of billions of rubles in state funding. Authorities in Russia’s far eastern Primorye region have opened specialized summer military camps for 14-to-17-year-olds with names like ‘Stormtrooper’ and ‘Infantryman.’ Russia’s federal budget has allocated a record 70 billion rubles this year for “patriotic education” through the national project “Youth and Children” — a twenty-fold increase since 2021. Meanwhile, enrollment in formal military cadet schools and specialized recruitment tracks reached 780,000 students by 2025, up from 200,000 in 2018. Russian schools all start the new academic year on Sept. 1, known as the Day of Knowledge. Putin has marked the occasion in recent years by leading a lesson with children called “Conversations About Important Things.”  The obligatory weekly hour-long class was introduced in September 2022 to promote the Kremlin’s views on patriotism and Russian history including the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. An adapted version based on play is being introduced in kindergartens this year for pre-school children. In the Russian-occupied areas of eastern and southern Ukraine, there’s a wholesale revision of education in schools that amounts to cultural erasure. New state-approved history textbooks introduced this year will teach children in Moscow-controlled parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson regions that their land was always Russian. “The entire system has been reshuffled to normalize the war,” said Alexandra Arkhipova, a Russian anthropologist and researcher at the Ecole Normale Superieure in Paris. “The state is preparing young people to accept the battlefield as their primary civic destination.”

items.title: MLB roundup: Dodgers prevail in Tarik Skubal's return to Detroit
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Freddie Freeman drove in the go-ahead run during the eighth inning in Tarik Skubal's return to Detroit as the Los Angeles Dodgers edged the slumping Tigers 2-1 on Friday.
items.body:
Freddie Freeman drove in the go-ahead run during the eighth inning in Tarik Skubal's return to Detroit as the Los Angeles Dodgers edged the slumping Tigers 2-1 on Friday.
Skubal gave up one run on four hits while striking out seven in six innings. The two-time Cy Young Award winner was dealt by the Tigers to the Dodgers earlier this month. Evan Phillips (2-2) struck out all three batters he faced and earned the win, and Tanner Scott pitched the ninth for his 20th save.
Miguel Rojas drove in the other Los Angeles run with a pinch-hit single in the sixth as the Dodgers snapped a three-game losing streak.
Detroit starter Drew Anderson held the Dodgers, who left 15 men on base, scoreless over 4 2/3 innings despite giving up four hits and walking five. Max Clark's triple knocked in the lone run for the Tigers, who took their eighth loss in nine games.
Phillies 5, Angels 3
Pinch hitter Edmundo Sosa hit a go-ahead grand slam with two outs in the top of the ninth inning as Philadelphia rallied past Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif.
Angels reliever Sammy Peralta entered with the bases loaded to face Sosa, who delivered his first career grand slam. Luis Arraez and Kyle Schwarber each had two hits for the Phillies, who won for the 11th time in 13 games.
Wade Meckler went 1-for-3 with a walk, an RBI, a run and a homer-saving catch for the Angels, who took their fifth straight loss.
Yankees 1, Red Sox 0
Cam Schlittler withstood five walks in 5 2/3 innings and Yankees outfielders started a pair of double plays during New York's victory over visiting Boston.
Paul Goldschmidt homered off Boston starter Patrick Sandoval (1-3) in the third inning. Schlittler (12-6) allowed two hits, struck out eight and lowered his AL-leading ERA to 2.09. David Bednar recorded a 1-2-3 ninth for his 31st save.
Sandoval gave up one run on three hits over 5 1/3 innings as the Red Sox took their second loss in a row.
Reds 10, Cubs 8
Tyler Stephenson belted a three-run homer and Sal Stewart drove in two runs to set the franchise rookie record for RBIs in a season, fueling visiting Cincinnati to a victory over Chicago.
Stewart went deep in the fifth inning for his team-leading 29th homer of the season. It also marked his 101st RBI, snapping a tie for the franchise rookie record that Jim Greengrass set in 1953. Cincinnati scored 10 runs for the second straight game to make a winner out of Rhett Lowder (6-8), who allowed three runs in five innings.
Pedro Ramirez belted a three-run homer, Michael Busch hit a two-run shot and Seiya Suzuki joined Nico Hoerner in collecting three hits apiece for the Cubs, who have lost six of their past eight games.
Brewers 6, Rangers 1
Logan Henderson was nearly perfect for host Milwaukee, which beat Texas for its third straight win.
Henderson (9-2) faced 22 batters over seven innings, with Danny Jansen's third-inning homer the only blemish on his stat line. He struck out seven while tying his career high in innings pitched. Christian Yelich finished 3-for-5 for the Brewers, and William Contreras drove in three while going 2-for-4.
Cody Bradford (0-3) yielded three runs on nine hits in 5 2/3 innings as the Rangers took their third loss in a row.
Royals 3, Guardians 0
Michael Wacha struck out 10 over eight innings and Carter Jensen hit a two-run homer in the ninth, sending red-hot Kansas City to a victory at Cleveland.
Wacha (8-8) allowed four singles and did not issue a walk in tying his longest start of the season. He only permitted one runner to get past first base over 103 pitches. The right-hander powered Kansas City to its 11th win in 12 games.
The Guardians had their seven-game winning streak snapped. Cleveland starter Tanner Bibee (5-14) tied the Baltimore Orioles' Shane Baz for the major league lead in losses, giving up one run on seven hits in six innings.
Astros 3, Mets 1
Hunter Brown struck out a season-high 10 over 6 2/3 solid innings as visiting Houston beat New York.
Daulton Varsho had the go-ahead two-run single in the sixth as the Astros won for the third time in four games. Brown (4-3) yielded one run on five hits, and Josh Hader notched his 20th save with a 1-2-3 ninth.
Christian Scott (4-4) gave up three runs on one hit and five walks in 5 1/3 innings as the Mets dropped their third game in a row.
White Sox 7, Twins 4
Colson Montgomery went 2-for-4 with a homer and three RBIs as Chicago recorded a win over Minnesota in Minneapolis.
Andrew Benintendi finished 2-for-4 with a double and two RBIs for the White Sox, who won their third straight game. Grant Taylor (7-2) pitched 2 2/3 scoreless innings of relief, and Bryan Hudson tossed a scoreless ninth for his sixth save.
Brooks Lee and Kody Clemens each homered and singled for the Twins, and Walker Jenkins had a hit and a walk in his big-league debut. Dean Kremer (2-5) allowed six runs (five earned) on seven hits over four-plus innings.
Braves 6, Rockies 4
Michael Harris II homered, doubled and drove in three runs, Ronald Acuna Jr. added three hits and three runs, and host Atlanta beat Colorado.
Mauricio Dubon and Sean Murphy each had two hits and an RBI to back five solid innings by Atlanta starter Grant Holmes (9-5). The right-hander allowed three runs on eight hits for the Braves, who have won five in a row. Raisel Iglesias got the final three outs for his 29th save.
Hunter Goodman had three hits and an RBI while Zac Veen and Mickey Moniak had two hits apiece for Colorado, which fell to 2-3 on its seven-game road trip. Rockies starter Tomoyuki Sugano (12-8) allowed six runs on 10 hits over four-plus innings.
Cardinals 4, Pirates 1
Rookie Quinn Mathews pitched effectively into the sixth inning for his first major league victory and Jimmy Crooks hit a two-run homer for St. Louis, which beat visiting Pittsburgh.
Jordan Walker added three hits and scored twice for the Cardinals, who had lost five of six. Mathews (1-2) allowed a run on five hits over 5 2/3 innings. Ryne Stanek pitched a perfect ninth for his second save.
Jared Jones (2-6) permitted three runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings for the Pirates, who committed three errors. Pittsburgh has scored a total of five runs in the past five games.
Blue Jays 8, Mariners 1
George Springer went 4-for-4 with a solo homer as Toronto defeated visiting Seattle.
Nathan Lukes and Kazuma Okamoto added solo shots for the Blue Jays. Okamoto had three RBIs. Dylan Cease (9-5) allowed one run, four hits and one walk while striking out eight in six innings as Toronto earned just its second win in five games.
Dominic Canzone stroked a solo homer for the Mariners while going 2-for-4. Randy Arozarena had a single and two walks as Seattle took its second loss in a row. Emerson Hancock (7-8) was tagged for five runs on eight hits in five innings.
Nationals 9, Marlins 2
Brady House smacked a three-run homer while Jackson Kent pitched seven innings of one-run ball to earn his first major league win as Washington beat visiting Miami.
Harry Ford also homered and Abimelec Ortiz had two hits for the Nationals, who have won consecutive games for the first time since a three-game run Aug. 7-9. Kent (1-2) gave up three hits, walked four and struck out three while throwing 106 pitches.
Heriberto Hernandez homered for the Marlins, who had won eight straight games against the Nationals. Eury Perez (7-10) surrendered five runs on two hits in three innings.
Rays 9, Padres 4
Yandy Diaz went 2-for-5 with a home run and two RBIs for Tampa Bay, which produced a five-run fourth inning to breeze past San Diego in St. Petersburg, Fla.
Chandler Simpson went 2-for-4 with a double, two runs and two stolen bases for the Rays. Cedric Mullins homered, scored twice and drove in two runs. Shane McClanahan (10-6) pitched 5 2/3 innings and allowed four runs, three earned, on three hits.
Jackson Merrill went 2-for-3, stroked a two-run homer, walked and scored twice for the Padres. Casey Mize (5-8) surrendered seven runs, two earned, on six hits over five innings.
Orioles 4, Athletics 3 (10 innings)
Coby Mayo and Christian Encarnacion-Strand each singled home a run in the 10th inning as Baltimore beat the Athletics in West Sacramento, Calif.
Brandon Young tossed seven innings of one-run ball for the Orioles, who won for the third time in four games. Andrew Kittredge (3-3) pitched a scoreless ninth inning, and Alex Hoppe allowed a run in the 10th but logged his first career save.
The A's, who had won four of their previous five games, got a homer from Jonah Heim. Brady Basso (0-1) yielded the decisive runs in the 10th.
Diamondbacks 10, Giants 6
Lars Nootbaar hit the first pitch of the game for a home run, Corbin Carroll and Tim Tawa went deep in a five-run third inning, and visiting Arizona overpowered San Francisco.
Nootbaar collected three hits for the Diamondbacks, who moved within a half-game of the National League's third and final wild-card spot. The Diamondbacks bullpen threw five innings and allowed just one unearned run and one hit, with Gerardo Carrillo (3-1) getting the win.
Bryce Eldridge and Christian Koss launched homers for the Giants, who took their ninth loss in 11 meetings with Arizona this season. Blade Tidwell (0-1) went five innings, allowing six runs on seven hits.
--Field Level Media

items.author: Reuters

items.summary: One of the main players in a struggle to agree a restructuring plan for Volkswagen AG , Lower Saxony state Premier Olaf Lies, said there was heavy pressure on all sides to reach an agreement in the next few days.
items.body:
One of the main players in a struggle to agree a restructuring plan for Volkswagen AG , Lower Saxony state Premier Olaf Lies, said there was heavy pressure on all sides to reach an agreement in the next few days.
The supervisory board of Europe's largest automaker is due to meet on September 4 to [USN:L8N44O1C5 TEXT:"discuss a turnaround plan"] potentially involving tens of thousands of additional job losses. The issue has pitted VW's management against unions and the German state, its second-biggest shareholder.
"I strongly urge that we use the time remaining until the next meeting to bring the different positions together," he told a briefing with journalists on Friday.
He said the business challenges facing Volkswagen, which has struggled in the face of costly tariffs, falling demand and mounting competition from China, needed to be handled urgently. But he said the group's position in the wider industrial landscape also had to be considered.
"With its sites in Lower Saxony and across Germany, its tens of thousands of employees and their families, and its suppliers and service providers, Volkswagen also bears an enormous responsibility for the wider economy and society," he said.
VW Chief Executive Oliver Blume [USN:L8N44M0FW TEXT:"wants to double"] planned job cuts to as many as 50,000, possibly close factories and spin off some company divisions in a radical drive to slash costs across the group.
That has triggered fierce opposition from unions and strong concern from Lower Saxony, which has an effective blocking minority shareholding.
The two sides are seeking a compromise likely to centre on the scale of job cuts and future plans for factories that are at risk, according to sources familiar with the discussions.
"I am convinced that we must find a viable solution here," Lies said. He said VW had always combined economic prudence with social responsibility, "and the solution we are now seeking should be measured against that standard."
VW's executive committee, which includes VW's works council chief, as well as Lies and members of the Porsche and Piech shareholder families, is set to convene on Thursday, a day ahead of the supervisory board meeting, to see where things stand.

items.title: Alcaraz says uncertainty over comeback fuelled 'intrusive thoughts'
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz said "intrusive thoughts" about the timing of his return were the toughest part of a wrist injury layoff that sidelined him for nearly five months ahead of his U.S. Open title defence.
items.body:
Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz said "intrusive thoughts" about the timing of his return were the toughest part of a wrist injury layoff that sidelined him for nearly five months ahead of his U.S. Open title defence.
The 23-year-old Spaniard, who became the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam when he claimed his seventh major title at this year's Australian Open, returns to Flushing Meadows with limited match practice but familiar expectations as he chases a third title in New York.
Alcaraz missed most of the clay season and was also forced to sit out the French Open, Wimbledon and the North American hardcourt swing due to the injury. He made his competitive return earlier this week in the U.S. Open mixed doubles alongside 23-times singles Grand Slam champion Serena Williams.
"The first month was kind of difficult for me because I couldn't do anything with my right arm. It was tough," Alcaraz told reporters on Friday.
"But at the same time, I enjoyed my time with family, friends and staying at home.
"But once I started to practice a little bit, that I didn't know when I'm going to start, that thoughts are really difficult to deal with, because I don't know if I'm going to be ready for Cincinnati, for U.S. Open, or I'm going to miss the whole American swing.
"But finally, here we are. My goal was try to be healthy as soon as possible and try not to miss more competitions. So I would say that intrusive thoughts were the most difficult things to deal with in this process."
The second seed opens his campaign against Russia's Roman Safiullin, ranked 98th in the world, and could face either Arthur Fils or Ben Shelton in the quarter-finals before a potential semi-final clash with 24-times Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic, 2021 U.S. Open champion Daniil Medvedev, Frances Tiafoe or Brandon Nakashima.
The tournament will also be missing world number one Jannik Sinner, Alcaraz's biggest rival, after the 25-year-old Italian withdrew with a persistent right knee injury.
"We are not going to see each other for about six months or seven months now. So it's kind of a weird situation," Alcaraz said. "I just wish him all the best. Hopefully a really great recovery and see him back on court at his best once again..."
The U.S. Open men's and women's singles main draws get under way on Sunday.

BEIJING: The threat of a lake formed after a glacier collapse bursting near the China-Nepal border where a devastating flood occurred earlier this week has decreased, Chinese authorities said on Saturday (Aug 29), as its size appears to have shrunk.
Satellite images from Thursday to Saturday morning suggest that water in the lake - straddling the China-Nepal border at the confluence of two rivers - has been slowly flowing through, decreasing the reservoir gradually, state broadcaster CCTV reported citing the Water Resources Ministry.
The ministry said satellite imagery of the surface area of the lake at Purepu Tsangpo river showed it was 99,000 sqm in size on early Saturday morning - around the size of 14 football fields combined - having shrunk by 21,000 sqm compared with images from Thursday.
A glacier collapse on Wednesday sending a powerful torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris through Himalayan mountain river systems swept away a border port complex linking China's Tibet to Nepal, killing hundreds and leaving thousands missing .

Experts and authorities have warned of the extremely high risk of secondary disasters in the valley, especially from the lake that was formed by glacier debris, potentially endangering rescue operations downstream.
State-owned engineering and rescue enterprise China Anneng, which has been monitoring the lake since Thursday, dispatched a 15-member team on Friday with reconnaissance drones, portable satellite stations and mobile surveillance cameras to gather more data about the lake.
An overflow from the lake on Friday temporarily halted rescue work before further assessment deemed the risks manageable.
Authorities have also flagged another larger body of water at the bottom of the glacier collapse.
"We estimate its area to be over 120,000 square meters, but its depth is currently unknown," said Chen Hongqi, a senior engineer at the Ministry of Natural Resources' Geological Disaster Technical Guidance Center.
Flood risks will remain until the two lakes have fully drained, an official with Nepal's Disaster Management Authority has said.

In bleak rainy weather on Saturday morning, more than 50 rescue workers combed through the grey rubble of boulders and mud looking for signs of life and calling out to any survivors, according to CCTV.
The first team of rescuers and a search-and-rescue dog had made their way to the location of the Gyirong border crossing complex on Friday afternoon, which they described as having nothing left but ruins.
Dangerous conditions at the main disaster zone, made more complex as roads and communication were cut off, continue to pose challenges to the Chinese relief efforts, state news agency Xinhua said.
China's death count from the disaster rose to seven early Saturday, with 554 still missing .
Nearly 500 villagers and construction workers, as well as all 555 tourists from the area have been evacuated, Xinhua said.

items.body:
UP: Health Department in Varanasi issues guidelines to prevent Swine Flu He has directed them to reserve the required number of beds at district-level hospitals as well as all community health centres and to ensure the availability of essential medicines used in the treatment of swine flu.
ANI | Updated: 29-08-2026 19:21 IST | Created: 29-08-2026 19:21 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Chief Medical Officer (CMO) of Varanasi, Dr NP Singh, has issued necessary guidelines to health department officials to prevent swine flu (Influenza-A/H1N1) and to raise public awareness about the disease. He has directed them to reserve the required number of beds at district-level hospitals as well as all community health centres and to ensure the availability of essential medicines used in the treatment of swine flu.
The CMO stated that swine flu is a contagious respiratory disease. It can spread through contact with respiratory droplets emitted by an infected person coughing, sneezing, or speaking. Therefore, timely identification of symptoms and appropriate treatment are crucial. These are the main symptoms of swine flu. A person infected with swine flu may typically experience fever, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, headache, body and muscle aches, extreme fatigue, and weakness. In some cases, vomiting or diarrhoea may also occur.
It is especially important to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms appear in the elderly, young children, pregnant women, and those with pre-existing medical conditions. Keep these things in mind for prevention: Cover your nose and mouth with a handkerchief or tissue when coughing or sneezing.
Wash your hands regularly with soap and water or use hand sanitiser. Avoid crowded places if you have a fever, cough, or other respiratory symptoms. Avoid contact with infected or sick people. Do not dispose of used tissues in public. Get adequate rest and drink plenty of fluids. Do not take antibiotics or other medications without medical advice, the CMO said. Instructions to upload information of symptomatic individuals on the portal: CMO Singh has directed all concerned officials and health centre in-charges to ensure timely identification, medical examination, treatment, and referral, as needed, of individuals with swine flu symptoms. Necessary information related to such identified individuals should be uploaded in a timely manner to the designated portal to ensure effective monitoring and control of the disease at the district level. He has also directed regular reviews of the availability of essential medicines, testing, and treatment resources at health institutions.
The Chief Medical Officer has appealed to the public not to panic if they notice swine flu symptoms, but to seek timely medical advice. Ignore any rumours regarding the disease and seek treatment only as directed by a doctor. Swine flu infection can be effectively controlled through caution, hygiene, and timely treatment. Dos and Don'ts: Wash hands frequently with soap. Cover your mouth when coughing/sneezing. Seek medical advice if you have symptoms. Get adequate rest and fluids. What not to do: Do not take medicine without medical advice. Avoid crowds if you have symptoms. Do not ignore the illness. Do not believe rumours. (ANI)

items.title: Norway mourns King Harald as crowds gather at royal palace
items.author: Nerijus Adomaitis, Janis Laizans
items.creator: Nerijus Adomaitis, Janis Laizans
items.summary: Thousands of Norwegians gathered on Saturday to say goodbye to King Harald in front of the royal palace, where he lies in state, with many well-wishers remembering his sense of inclusiveness and tolerance.
items.body:
Thousands of Norwegians gathered on Saturday to say goodbye to King Harald in front of the royal palace, where he lies in state, with many well-wishers remembering his sense of inclusiveness and tolerance.
Europe's oldest monarch, who emerged from the shadow of his well-loved, extrovert father to become a reformer during more than three decades on the throne, [USN:L6N44P0J6 TEXT:"died on Friday"] at the age of 89.
Late on Friday, throngs lined the streets of Oslo in pouring rain to watch the funeral cortege travel from Oslo University Hospital, where Harald died, to the royal palace.
Flags were flying at half-mast throughout the country and portraits of the late king in gala uniform were everywhere, from bus stops, trams and metro stations to shops, offices and public buildings.
As the nation mourned Harald, attention also turned to the succession. Crown Prince Haakon, the late king's only son, automatically became king upon his father's death under Norway's constitutional monarchy.
[USN:L8N3H10JJ TEXT:"King Haakon VIII"] will speak to the nation in a televised address at 1900 local time (1700 GMT) on Saturday. On Tuesday, he [USN:L8N3IG0RD TEXT:"will take the oath"] in front of parliament, when he will swear to defend Norway's constitution and laws.
He became king the moment his father passed away. There will be no coronation as they were abolished by parliament in 1908.
TOLERANCE AND INCLUSIVENESS The main avenue in central Oslo, Karl Johan, was tightly packed with Norwegians of all walks of life heading towards the palace, clutching flowers, handwritten cards, drawings and small national flags.
On what should have been the 58th wedding anniversary of Harald and Queen Sonja, who survives him, they praised the late king's spirit of inclusiveness.
"He meant a lot to us immigrants ... We felt really very included. So, thanks to him, I feel so Norwegian," Veselina Vitanova, a 43-year-old teacher originally from Bulgaria, told Reuters outside the palace.
Another referred to a speech Harald delivered in 2016 that went viral worldwide, in which he said: "Norwegians are girls who love girls, boys who love boys and girls and boys who love each other".
"It embodies the way he felt about people and the way he wanted us Norwegians to feel about each other," said Mari Eidsvaag, 32, who wore a T-shirt emblazoned with that sentence, a rainbow and a drawing of King Harald.
"I think it's a very important statement, especially these days," she told Reuters.

items.title: ネパール・中国土石流、なお約3000人不明　死者600人超
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [カトマンズ ２９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[カトマンズ ２９日 ロイター] - ネパール当局は２９日、中国チベット自治区との国境地帯を襲った大規模土石流の捜索・救助活動を悪天候のために中断した。またワグル財務相は、政府による初期の試算で、復興に４０─５０億ドルが必要になるとロイターに語った。

当局によると、２６日に発生した土石流と洪水では、これまでにネパールで少なくとも６２６人、中国チベット自治区で７人が死亡した。行方不明者は約３０００人に上り、ネパールで約２４２６人、チベット自治区の吉隆県で少なくとも５５８人。うち外国人が約５４０人含まれ、その多くはインドからのヒンズー教巡礼者だという。

被害の大きいラスワ郡の高官は２９日、「雨が降り、霧がかかっているため、捜索・救助活動を一時的に停止した」と語った。前日も、災害原因とみられる氷河崩落で形成された湖が越水したことなどから、救助が一時中断した。

この湖は、ネパール当局が監視している洪水発生地点の上流にある２つの湖のうちの一つ。当局者は、両湖が完全に排水されるまで洪水リスクは続くと警告した。

中国国営の新華社通信は２８日、当局の分析によると、うち１つの湖は縮小しつつあると伝えた。ただ、中国政府の地質災害専門家はこの湖について、不安定な状態にある可能性を指摘。周辺に点在する１００以上の氷河湖も脅威となり得ると述べた。

ネパールのカナル外相は、捜索・救助活動そのものに支援は必要ないとしつつ、トンネルに閉じ込められた人々の救出、橋が破壊された地域での輸送・通信網の復旧、遺体の身元確認、ＤＮＡ鑑定、遺体の長期保管については技術的な支援が必要だと述べた。

ワグル財務相は２８日、ロイターの取材に、災害からの復興に必要な費用は初期試算で４０億─５０億ドルの規模になるとの見通しを示した。「あくまで試算に過ぎず、被害状況は現在評価中だ」と述べた。

約９０００人が死亡し、ネパール史上最悪の自然災害となった２０１５年の大地震では復興費が９０億ドルに上ったが、現時点でそれよりは少ない額になるだろうと述べた。

items.title: Leao bids emotional farewell to Milan amid reports of Galatasaray switch
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Portugal winger Rafael Leao bid an emotional farewell to AC Milan amid reports he is close to joining Turkish side Galatasaray, saying the decision was difficult but that he would always remain part of the Rossoneri's history.
items.body:
Portugal winger Rafael Leao bid an emotional farewell to AC Milan amid reports he is close to joining Turkish side Galatasaray, saying the decision was difficult but that he would always remain part of the Rossoneri's history.
A product of Sporting Portugal's academy, the 27-year-old has been capped 49 times by his country and represented Portugal at the 2022 and 2026 World Cups. He joined Milan from French side Lille in 2019.
Leao became a key figure for the seven-time European champions, scoring 80 goals and providing 65 assists in 291 appearances across all competitions. He helped Milan win the Serie A title in 2021-22 and the Italian Super Cup in the 2024-25 season.
According to media reports, Milan have accepted a €45 million ($52.12 million) offer from Galatasaray for Leao, whose contract with the Italian club runs until June 2028.
"It's a difficult time," Leao told Sky Sport Italy on Friday after Milan's 2-0 Serie A win over Venezia at the San Siro, where he was not part of the squad. "I've said goodbye to my teammates after seven years.
"Milan helped me grow and understand what top-flight football is all about. The time has come to say goodbye. I might have liked to say goodbye in a different way. The fans supported me even during the tough times.
"I know what I've achieved here; I'll go down in the club's history. All I can do is say thank you."
Milan appointed former Manchester United coach [USN:L6N42O13Y TEXT:"Ruben Amorim"] as manager in June after a disappointing campaign last season that saw them miss out on Champions League qualification.
They have since made a strong start to the new Serie A season, winning their opening two matches.
"My love for Milan will never end; even from afar, I'll always be watching them...," Leao added.
"There are times when you have to make a decision and choose a different path.
"Today, Milan showed great quality and have a great manager. He's someone who can help Milan win major trophies. It's the sort of football I like...
"Life doesn't end here. I cried; I was moved."
($1 = 0.8634 euros)

items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) has increased its second-quarter employee bonuses by more than 50 percent from a year earlier, as the world's largest contract chipmaker posted record ...
items.body:
TSMC's Q2 employee bonuses rise more than 50% year-on-year Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) has increased its second-quarter employee bonuses by more than 50 percent from a year earlier, as the world's largest contract chipmaker posted record earnings in the three-month period, Focus Taiwan CNA English News reported.
ANI | Updated: 29-08-2026 18:45 IST | Created: 29-08-2026 18:45 IST

The logo of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is displayed at its fabrication plant in Kaohsiung, Taiwan. (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) has increased its second-quarter employee bonuses by more than 50 percent from a year earlier, as the world's largest contract chipmaker posted record earnings in the three-month period, Focus Taiwan CNA English News reported. TSMC distributed its second-quarter bonuses to employees on Friday. According to the chipmaker's financial data, employee bonuses for the April-June period totaled NT$36 billion (US$1.14 billion), up more than 50 percent from a year earlier.
During the April-June period, TSMC posted NT$706.56 billion in net profit, up 77.4 percent from a year earlier and 23.4 percent from a quarter earlier, according to Focus Taiwan CNA English News. Second-quarter earnings per share (EPS) rose to NT$27.25, compared with NT$15.36 a year earlier and NT$22.08 in the first quarter, TSMC said.
The record quarterly net profit reflected strong global demand for high-performance computing devices, Internet of Things applications and consumer electronics products, according to TSMC. TSMC's financial data also showed that employee bonuses for the first half of this year totaled NT$70.35 billion, up 54.3 percent from a year earlier.
In the first six months of this year, TSMC posted NT$1.28 trillion in net profit, up 68.3 percent from a year earlier, while EPS rose to NT$49.32 from NT$29.30 a year earlier, Focus Taiwan CNA English News reported. With TSMC allocating more of its profits to enhance social sustainability as part of its efforts to give back to Taiwan, growth in employee bonuses lagged behind the increase in net profit during the six-month period. Nevertheless, the increase so far this year exceeded the roughly 30 percent growth recorded in 2025.
Sources said TSMC distributes half of its employee bonuses on a quarterly basis and pays the remaining half after the shareholders' meeting the following year. (ANI)

items.title: Risk of lake burst near China-Nepal disaster site wanes
items.author: Liz Lee, Yukun Zhang
items.creator: Liz Lee, Yukun Zhang
items.summary: Satellite images suggest that water is slowly flowing out.
items.body:
The threat of a lake formed after a glacier collapse bursting near the China-Nepal border, where a devastating flood struck earlier this week, has eased, Chinese authorities said on Saturday, as it appears to have shrunk.
Satellite images from Thursday to Saturday morning suggest that water in the lake, which straddles the border between China's Tibet region and Nepal at the confluence of two rivers, has been slowly flowing out and gradually reducing the reservoir, state broadcaster CCTV reported, citing the Water Resources Ministry.
By Saturday afternoon, parts of the lake bed had become visible, CCTV reported.
The ministry said satellite imagery of the lake on the Purepu Tsangpo river showed it covered 99,000 square metres (1.1 million square feet) early on Saturday, roughly the size of 14 soccer pitches, having shrunk by 21,000 square metres since Thursday.
A glacier collapse on Wednesday sent a torrent of rock, ice, mud and debris through Himalayan river systems, sweeping away a border port complex linking Tibet with Nepal, killing hundreds and leaving thousands missing.
RISKS UNDER WATCH Experts and authorities have warned of an extremely high risk of secondary disasters in the valley, particularly from the lake formed by glacier debris, which could threaten rescue operations downstream.
With water draining naturally, Water Resources Ministry experts said search and rescue operations downstream could continue safely if outflows remain low or manageable and recede completely within two to three days.
Rescue workers could be notified promptly to evacuate if any abnormalities appear at the lake, with warnings issued more than 30 minutes in advance, CCTV cited the experts as saying.
State-owned engineering and rescue company China Anneng, which has been monitoring the lake since Thursday, has deployed radar and drones around the lake for 24-hour surveillance, CCTV said.
Initial [USN:L6N44P07I TEXT:"overflow"] from the lake on Friday temporarily halted rescue work before a subsequent assessment deemed the risks manageable.
Authorities have also flagged another, larger body of water at the foot of the glacier collapse.
"We estimate its area to be over 120,000 square metres, but its depth is currently unknown," said Chen Hongqi, a senior engineer at the Ministry of Natural Resources' Geological Disaster Technical Guidance Center.
Flood risks will [USN:L6N44P0OC TEXT:"remain"] until both lakes have fully drained, an official with Nepal's Disaster Management Authority has said.
LOOKING FOR SURVIVORS In bleak, rainy conditions on Saturday morning, more than 50 rescue workers combed through rubble of boulders and mud, looking for signs of life and calling out for survivors, CCTV reported.
The first rescue team and a search dog reached the Gyirong border crossing complex on Friday afternoon and found it [USN:L6N44P04B TEXT:"reduced to ruins"].
Dangerous conditions at the main disaster zone, compounded by damaged roads and disrupted communications, continue to hamper Chinese relief efforts, state news agency Xinhua said.
Forecasts show intermittent rain in the area over the next three days.
Authorities are racing to reopen a key highway leading to the border port. By Saturday afternoon, crews had advanced within about 1.5 km (0.93 mile) of the site.
China's death toll rose to seven early on Saturday, with 554 people still missing.
Nearly 500 villagers and construction workers, along with 555 tourists in the area, have been evacuated, Xinhua said.
CAUSE STILL UNCLEAR The cause of the collapse remains unclear, but climate experts say global warming could be a factor.
"We're still not absolutely sure whether it was triggered by an earthquake or ... by warm temperatures melting the glacier," said Benjamin Horton, dean of the School of Energy and Environment at the City University of Hong Kong.
Videos shared on social media and verified by Reuters show the lower section of the glacier near the Langtang Lirung mountain peak breaking away and plunging into the valley below, triggering an avalanche of ice and rock and a massive landslide.
"One of the reasons why we don't fully understand the mechanisms that cause the landslide is that we have a lack of data. So there has to be this investment in the science, there has to be this investment in society," Horton said.
